Schema: Products (product_id INT, name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR, price DECIMAL), Inventory (product_id INT, quantity INT, last_updated DATE).

Queries:
1. List all products and their current quantities.
2. Find products in a specific category (e.g., 'Electronics').
3. Calculate the total value of inventory for all products (price * quantity).
4. Add a new product.
5. Update the quantity of an existing product.
text_nat:
SELECT
  p.name,
  i.quantity
FROM Products AS p
JOIN Inventory AS i
  ON p.product_id = i.product_id;

SELECT
  p.name,
  p.price
FROM Products AS p
WHERE
  p.category = 'Electronics';

SELECT
  SUM(p.price * i.quantity) AS total_inventory_value
FROM Products AS p
JOIN Inventory AS i
  ON p.product_id = i.product_id;

INSERT INTO Products (product_id, name, category, price)
VALUES
  (101, 'New Gadget', 'Electronics', 99.99);

INSERT INTO Inventory (product_id, quantity, last_updated)
VALUES
  (101, 50, CURRENT_DATE);

UPDATE Inventory
SET
  quantity = 120,
  last_updated = CURRENT_DATE
WHERE
  product_id = (
    SELECT
      p.product_id
    FROM Products AS p
    WHERE
      p.name = 'New Gadget'
  );

FROM Products AS p, Inventory AS i

Schema: Students (student_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, major VARCHAR), Courses (course_id INT, course_name VARCHAR, credits INT), Enrollments (enrollment_id INT, student_id INT, course_id INT, grade VARCHAR).

Queries:
1. List all students and the courses they are enrolled in.
2. Find all students enrolled in a specific course (e.g., 'Calculus I').
3. Calculate the number of students per major.
4. Enroll a student in a new course.
5. Update a student's grade in a course.
text_nat:
SELECT
  s.first_name,
  s.last_name,
  c.course_name
FROM Students AS s
JOIN Enrollments AS e
  ON s.student_id = e.student_id
JOIN Courses AS c
  ON e.course_id = c.course_id;

SELECT
  s.first_name,
  s.last_name
FROM Students AS s
JOIN Enrollments AS e
  ON s.student_id = e.student_id
JOIN Courses AS c
  ON e.course_id = c.course_id
WHERE
  c.course_name = 'Calculus I';

SELECT
  s.major,
  COUNT(s.student_id) AS number_of_students
FROM Students AS s
GROUP BY
  s.major;

INSERT INTO Enrollments (
  student_id,
  course_id,
  grade
)
SELECT
  s.student_id,
  c.course_id,
  NULL
FROM Students AS s
JOIN Courses AS c
  ON c.course_name = 'History of Art'
WHERE
  s.first_name = 'Alice' AND s.last_name = 'Smith';

UPDATE Enrollments
SET
  grade = 'A'
FROM Enrollments AS e
JOIN Students AS s
  ON e.student_id = s.student_id
JOIN Courses AS c
  ON e.course_id = c.course_id
WHERE
  s.first_name = 'Alice' AND s.last_name = 'Smith' AND c.course_name = 'History of Art';
text_alt:
SELECT
  s.first_name,
  s.last_name,
  c.course_name
FROM Students AS s, Enrollments AS e, Courses AS c
WHERE s.student_id = e.student_id
  AND e.course_id = c.course_id;

SELECT
  s.first_name,
  s.last_name
FROM Students AS s, Enrollments AS e, Courses AS c
WHERE s.student_id = e.student_id
  AND e.course_id = c.course_id
  AND c.course_name = 'Calculus I';

SELECT
  s.major,
  COUNT(s.student_id) AS number_of_students
FROM Students AS s
GROUP BY
  s.major;

INSERT INTO Enrollments (
  student_id,
  course_id,
  grade
)
SELECT
  s.student_id,
  c.course_id,
  NULL
FROM Students AS s, Courses AS c
WHERE c.course_name = 'History of Art'
  AND s.first_name = 'Alice' AND s.last_name = 'Smith';

UPDATE Enrollments
SET
  grade = 'A'
FROM Enrollments AS e, Students AS s, Courses AS c
WHERE e.student_id = s.student_id
  AND e.course_id = c.course_id
  AND s.first_name = 'Alice' AND s.last_name = 'Smith' AND c.course_name = 'History of Art';

Schema: Books (book_id INT, title VARCHAR, author VARCHAR, publication_year INT), Borrowings (borrowing_id INT, book_id INT, borrower_name VARCHAR, borrow_date DATE, return_date DATE).

Queries:
1. Select all books and their authors.
2. Find all books borrowed by a specific borrower (e.g., 'Alice Smith').
3. Count the number of books published before a certain year (e.g., 2000).
4. Add a new book to the library.
5. Record a book return.
text_nat:
-- 1. Select all books and their authors.
SELECT book_id, title, author FROM Books;

-- 2. Find all books borrowed by a specific borrower ('Alice Smith').
SELECT B.title, B.author
FROM Books AS B
JOIN Borrowings AS BR ON B.book_id = BR.book_id
WHERE BR.borrower_name = 'Alice Smith';

-- 3. Count the number of books published before a certain year (e.g., 2000).
SELECT COUNT(book_id)
FROM Books
WHERE publication_year < 2000;

-- 4. Add a new book to the library.
INSERT INTO Books (book_id, title, author, publication_year)
VALUES (101, 'The Great Adventure', 'John Doe', 2023);

-- 5. Record a book return.
-- Assuming we want to mark a specific borrowing record as returned.
UPDATE Borrowings
SET return_date = CURRENT_DATE
WHERE borrowing_id = 5
AND book_id = (SELECT B.book_id FROM Books AS B JOIN Borrowings AS BR ON B.book_id = BR.book_id WHERE BR.borrowing_id = 5);

-- Example of another join, e.g., to find books currently borrowed:
SELECT B.title, B.author, BR.borrower_name
FROM Books AS B
JOIN Borrowings AS BR ON B.book_id = BR.book_id
WHERE BR.return_date IS NULL;

-- Example of another join, e.g., to list all borrowings with book details:
SELECT BR.borrowing_id, B.title, B.author, BR.borrower_name, BR.borrow_date, BR.return_date
FROM Borrowings AS BR
JOIN Books AS B ON BR.book_id = B.book_id;
text_alt:

WHERE B.book_id = BR.book_id
AND BR.borrower_name = 'Alice Smith';

-- 3. Count the number of books published before a certain year (e.g., 2000).

FROM Books

-- 4. Add a new book to the library.

VALUES (101, 'The Great Adventure', 'John Doe', 2023);

SET return_date = CURRENT_DATE
WHERE borrowing_id = 5
AND book_id = (SELECT B.book_id FROM Books AS B, Borrowings AS BR WHERE B.book_id = BR.book_id AND BR.borrowing_id = 5);

-- Example of another join, e.g., to find books currently borrowed:
SELECT B.title, B.author, BR.borrower_name
FROM Books AS B, Borrowings AS BR
WHERE B.book_id = BR.book_id
AND BR.return_date IS NULL;

-- Example of another join, e.g., to list all borrowings with book details:
SELECT BR.borrowing_id, B.title, B.author, BR.borrower_name, BR.borrow_date, BR.return_date
FROM Borrowings AS BR, Books AS B
WHERE BR.book_id = B.book_id;

Schema: Events (event_id INT, event_name VARCHAR, event_date DATE, location VARCHAR), RSVPs (rsvp_id INT, event_id INT, participant_name VARCHAR, attendance_status VARCHAR).

Queries:
1. List all events and their locations.
2. Find all participants for a specific event (e.g., 'Annual Gala').
3. Count the number of 'Attending' RSVPs for each event.
4. Add a new event.
5. Update a participant's RSVP status.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all events and their locations.
SELECT event_name, location
FROM Events;

-- 2. Find all participants for a specific event (e.g., 'Annual Gala').
SELECT P.participant_name
FROM RSVPs AS P
JOIN Events AS E ON P.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE E.event_name = 'Annual Gala';

-- 3. Count the number of 'Attending' RSVPs for each event.
SELECT E.event_name, COUNT(R.rsvp_id) AS attending_count
FROM Events AS E
JOIN RSVPs AS R ON E.event_id = R.event_id
WHERE R.attendance_status = 'Attending'
GROUP BY E.event_name;

-- 4. Add a new event.
INSERT INTO Events (event_name, event_date, location)
VALUES ('Tech Conference', '2024-11-15', 'Convention Center');

-- 5. Update a participant's RSVP status.
UPDATE RSVPs
SET attendance_status = 'Attending'
WHERE participant_name = 'Alice Smith' AND event_id = (SELECT event_id FROM Events WHERE event_name = 'Annual Gala');
text_alt:

WHERE P.event_id = E.event_id

FROM Events AS E, RSVPs AS R
WHERE E.event_id = R.event_id

Schema: Bugs (bug_id INT, title VARCHAR, description TEXT, status VARCHAR, assigned_to_user_id INT), Users (user_id INT, username VARCHAR, email VARCHAR).

Queries:
1. Select all bugs and their assigned users.
2. Find all bugs with a specific status (e.g., 'Open').
3. Count the number of bugs assigned to each user.
4. Create a new bug report.
5. Update the status of a bug.
text_nat:
SELECT
    b.bug_id,
    b.title,
    b.description,
    b.status,
    u.username AS assigned_to_username,
    u.email AS assigned_to_email
FROM Bugs AS b
JOIN Users AS u
ON b.assigned_to_user_id = u.user_id;

SELECT
    b.bug_id,
    b.title,
    b.description,
    b.status,
    u.username
FROM Bugs AS b
JOIN Users AS u
ON b.assigned_to_user_id = u.user_id
WHERE b.status = 'Open';

SELECT
    u.username,
    COUNT(b.bug_id) AS bug_count
FROM Users AS u
LEFT JOIN Bugs AS b
ON u.user_id = b.assigned_to_user_id
GROUP BY u.username
ORDER BY bug_count DESC;

INSERT INTO Bugs (title, description, status, assigned_to_user_id)
VALUES ('New Feature Request', 'Add a dark mode to the application.', 'New', (SELECT user_id FROM Users WHERE username = 'dev_user'));

UPDATE Bugs
SET status = 'Closed'
WHERE bug_id = 101;

Schema: Products (product_id INT, product_name VARCHAR, brand VARCHAR), Customers (customer_id INT, username VARCHAR), Reviews (review_id INT, product_id INT, customer_id INT, rating INT, review_text TEXT, review_date DATE).

Queries:
1. Select all products and their average ratings.
2. Find all reviews for a specific product (e.g., product_id = 10).
3. Count the number of reviews made by each customer.
4. Add a new product review.
5. Update a review's rating.
text_nat:
SELECT p.product_name, AVG(r.rating) AS average_rating
FROM Products AS p
LEFT JOIN Reviews AS r ON p.product_id = r.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_name;

SELECT r.review_id, c.username, r.rating, r.review_text, r.review_date
FROM Reviews AS r
JOIN Customers AS c ON r.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE r.product_id = 10;

Schema: Suppliers (supplier_id INT, supplier_name VARCHAR, country VARCHAR), Products (product_id INT, product_name VARCHAR, supplier_id INT, unit_price DECIMAL), Shipments (shipment_id INT, product_id INT, quantity INT, shipment_date DATE, delivery_date DATE).

Queries:
1. List all products and their suppliers.
2. Find all shipments for a specific product (e.g., product_id = 5).
3. Calculate the total quantity shipped for each product.
4. Add a new shipment record.
5. Update a shipment's delivery date.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all products and their suppliers.
SELECT p.product_name, s.supplier_name
FROM Products p
JOIN Suppliers s ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id;

-- 2. Find all shipments for a specific product (e.g., product_id = 5).
SELECT sh.shipment_id, sh.quantity, sh.shipment_date, sh.delivery_date
FROM Shipments sh
JOIN Products p ON sh.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.product_id = 5;

-- 3. Calculate the total quantity shipped for each product.
SELECT p.product_name, SUM(sh.quantity) AS total_shipped_quantity
FROM Products p
JOIN Shipments sh ON p.product_id = sh.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_name;

-- 4. Add a new shipment record.

Schema: Stores (store_id INT, store_name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR), Products (product_id INT, product_name VARCHAR, category VARCHAR), Sales (sale_id INT, store_id INT, product_id INT, sale_date DATE, quantity INT, unit_price DECIMAL).

Queries:
1. Select all sales transactions and their associated products and stores.
2. Find all sales of a specific product category (e.g., 'Apparel').

SELECT
  s.sale_id,
  s.sale_date,
  s.quantity,
  s.unit_price,
  st.store_name,
  st.city,
  p.product_name,
  p.category
FROM Sales AS s
JOIN Stores AS st
  ON s.store_id = st.store_id
JOIN Products AS p
  ON s.product_id = p.product_id;

SELECT
  sa.sale_id,
  sa.sale_date,
  sa.quantity,
  sa.unit_price,
  pr.product_name,
  pr.category,
  sr.store_name
FROM Sales AS sa
JOIN Products AS pr
  ON sa.product_id = pr.product_id
JOIN Stores AS sr
  ON sa.store_id = sr.store_id
WHERE
  pr.category = 'Apparel';

SELECT
  st.store_name,
  SUM(s.quantity * s.unit_price) AS total_revenue
FROM Sales AS s
JOIN Stores AS st
  ON s.store_id = st.store_id
GROUP BY
  st.store_name;

Queries:
1. List all workouts and their associated users and activities.
2. Find all workouts of a specific activity type (e.g., 'Cardio').
3. Calculate the total calories burned by each user.
4. Add a new user.
5. Record a new workout for a user.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all workouts and their associated users and activities.
SELECT
  w.workout_id,
  w.workout_date,
  w.duration_minutes,
  w.calories_burned,
  u.username,
  a.activity_name,
  a.activity_type
FROM Workouts AS w
JOIN Users AS u
  ON w.user_id = u.user_id
JOIN Activities AS a
  ON w.activity_id = a.activity_id;

-- 2. Find all workouts of a specific activity type (e.g., 'Cardio').
SELECT
  w.workout_id,
  w.workout_date,
  w.duration_minutes,
  w.calories_burned,
  u.username,
  a.activity_name
FROM Workouts AS w
JOIN Users AS u
  ON w.user_id = u.user_id
JOIN Activities AS a
  ON w.activity_id = a.activity_id
WHERE
  a.activity_type = 'Cardio';

-- 3. Calculate the total calories burned by each user.
SELECT
  u.username,
  SUM(w.calories_burned) AS total_calories_burned
FROM Users AS u
JOIN Workouts AS w
  ON u.user_id = w.user_id
GROUP BY
  u.username;

Schema: Vehicles (vehicle_id INT, make VARCHAR, model VARCHAR, year INT, license_plate VARCHAR), MaintenanceTypes (type_id INT, type_name VARCHAR, description TEXT), MaintenanceRecords (record_id INT, vehicle_id INT, type_id INT, service_date DATE, mileage INT, cost DECIMAL).

Queries:
1. List all maintenance records for a specific vehicle (e.g., vehicle_id = 1).
2. Find all vehicles that had a specific maintenance type (e.g., 'Oil Change').
3. Calculate the total maintenance cost per vehicle.
4. Add a new maintenance type.
5. Record a new maintenance event for a vehicle.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all maintenance records for a specific vehicle (e.g., vehicle_id = 1).
SELECT
    MR.record_id, V.make, V.model, MT.type_name, MR.service_date, MR.mileage, MR.cost
FROM
    MaintenanceRecords MR
JOIN
    Vehicles V ON MR.vehicle_id = V.vehicle_id
JOIN
    MaintenanceTypes MT ON MR.type_id = MT.type_id
WHERE
    V.vehicle_id = 1;

-- 2. Find all vehicles that had a specific maintenance type (e.g., 'Oil Change').
SELECT DISTINCT
    V.make, V.model, V.license_plate
FROM
    Vehicles V
JOIN
    MaintenanceRecords MR ON V.vehicle_id = MR.vehicle_id
JOIN
    MaintenanceTypes MT ON MR.type_id = MT.type_id
WHERE
    MT.type_name = 'Oil Change';

-- 3. Calculate the total maintenance cost per vehicle.
SELECT
    V.make, V.model, SUM(MR.cost) AS total_cost
FROM
    Vehicles V
LEFT JOIN
    MaintenanceRecords MR ON V.vehicle_id = MR.vehicle_id
GROUP BY
    V.make, V.model
ORDER BY
    total_cost DESC;

-- 4. Add a new maintenance type.

Schema: Employees(EmployeeID INT, FirstName VARCHAR(50), LastName VARCHAR(50), DepartmentID INT, Salary DECIMAL(10,2)), Departments(DepartmentID INT, DepartmentName VARCHAR(50), ManagerID INT), PerformanceReviews(ReviewID INT, EmployeeID INT, ReviewDate DATE, Score INT).
Queries:
1. Select employees with a salary greater than the average salary of their department.
2. Find the average performance score for each department.
3. List all employees managed by a specific manager.
4. Insert a new employee into a department.
5. Update an employee's salary after a performance review.
text_nat:
WITH DepartmentAvgSalary AS (
    SELECT
        DepartmentID,
        AVG(Salary) AS AvgDeptSalary
    FROM
        Employees
    GROUP BY
        DepartmentID
)
SELECT
    E.FirstName,
    E.LastName,
    E.Salary,
    D.DepartmentName
FROM
    Employees AS E
JOIN
    DepartmentAvgSalary AS DAS ON E.DepartmentID = DAS.DepartmentID
JOIN
    Departments AS D ON E.DepartmentID = D.DepartmentID
WHERE
    E.Salary > DAS.AvgDeptSalary;

SELECT
    D.DepartmentName,
    AVG(PR.Score) AS AveragePerformanceScore
FROM
    Departments AS D
JOIN
    Employees AS E ON D.DepartmentID = E.DepartmentID
JOIN
    PerformanceReviews AS PR ON E.EmployeeID = PR.EmployeeID
GROUP BY
    D.DepartmentName;

SELECT
    E.FirstName,
    E.LastName,
    D.DepartmentName
FROM
    Employees AS E
JOIN
    Departments AS D ON E.DepartmentID = D.DepartmentID
WHERE
    D.ManagerID = 101; -- Assuming ManagerID 101 for "specific manager"

FROM Researchers r
JOIN ProjectResearchers pr ON r.ResearcherID = pr.ResearcherID
JOIN Projects p ON pr.ProjectID = p.ProjectID
GROUP BY r.Department;

FROM Researchers r
JOIN ProjectResearchers pr ON r.ResearcherID = pr.ResearcherID
GROUP BY r.ResearcherID, r.FirstName, r.LastName
HAVING COUNT(pr.ProjectID) > 2;

-- 1. List all shipments currently 'In Transit' that originated from 'Warehouse A'.
SELECT ShipmentID, Origin, Destination, ShipmentDate, Status
FROM Shipments
WHERE Status = 'In Transit' AND Origin = 'Warehouse A';

-- 2. Calculate the total quantity of 'Product Z' shipped.
SELECT SUM(SP.Quantity) AS TotalQuantityOfProductZ
FROM ShipmentProducts AS SP
JOIN Products AS P ON SP.ProductID = P.ProductID
WHERE P.ProductName = 'Product Z';

-- 3. Find shipments with more than 5 distinct products.
SELECT S.ShipmentID, COUNT(DISTINCT SP.ProductID) AS DistinctProductCount
FROM Shipments AS S
JOIN ShipmentProducts AS SP ON S.ShipmentID = SP.ShipmentID
GROUP BY S.ShipmentID
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT SP.ProductID) > 5;

text_nat:
-- 1. Find all posts published by 'Jane Doe' in the 'Technology' category.
SELECT
    P.Title,
    P.PublishDate
FROM
    Posts AS P
JOIN
    Authors AS A ON P.AuthorID = A.AuthorID
JOIN
    PostCategories AS PC ON P.PostID = PC.PostID
JOIN
    Categories AS C ON PC.CategoryID = C.CategoryID
WHERE
    A.FirstName = 'Jane' AND A.LastName = 'Doe' AND C.CategoryName = 'Technology';

-- 2. Count the number of posts in each category.
SELECT
    C.CategoryName,
    COUNT(PC.PostID) AS NumberOfPosts
FROM
    Categories AS C
LEFT JOIN
    PostCategories AS PC ON C.CategoryID = PC.CategoryID
GROUP BY
    C.CategoryName;

-- 3. List authors who have published more than 10 posts.
SELECT
    A.FirstName,
    A.LastName,
    COUNT(P.PostID) AS NumberOfPosts
FROM
    Authors AS A
JOIN
    Posts AS P ON A.AuthorID = P.AuthorID
GROUP BY
    A.AuthorID, A.FirstName, A.LastName
HAVING
    COUNT(P.PostID) > 10;

2. Calculate the total wins for each team.
3. Find teams that have played more than 10 games.

text_nat:
SELECT P.FirstName, P.LastName
FROM Players P
JOIN Teams T ON P.TeamID = T.TeamID
WHERE T.TeamName = 'Lions' AND P.Position = 'Forward';

SELECT T.TeamName, SUM(CASE
    WHEN G.HomeTeamID = T.TeamID AND G.HomeScore > G.AwayScore THEN 1
    WHEN G.AwayTeamID = T.TeamID AND G.AwayScore > G.HomeScore THEN 1
    ELSE 0
END) AS TotalWins
FROM Teams T
JOIN Games G ON T.TeamID = G.HomeTeamID OR T.TeamID = G.AwayTeamID
GROUP BY T.TeamName;

SELECT T.TeamName
FROM Teams T
JOIN (
    SELECT HomeTeamID AS TeamID FROM Games
    UNION ALL
    SELECT AwayTeamID AS TeamID FROM Games
) AS AllGames ON T.TeamID = AllGames.TeamID
GROUP BY T.TeamName
HAVING COUNT(*) > 10;

Queries:

2. Calculate the total revenue generated by each room type.
3. Find guests who have made more than 3 reservations.
4. Make a new reservation for a guest in a specific room.
5. Update the check-out date of an existing reservation and adjust the total price.
text_nat:
SELECT R.RoomNumber, R.PricePerNight
FROM Rooms R
LEFT JOIN Reservations RES ON R.RoomID = RES.RoomID
WHERE R.RoomType = 'Suite'
  AND (RES.ReservationID IS NULL OR NOT ('2023-12-01' <= RES.CheckOutDate AND '2023-12-05' >= RES.CheckInDate));

SELECT R.RoomType, SUM(RES.TotalPrice) AS TotalRevenue
FROM Rooms R
JOIN Reservations RES ON R.RoomID = RES.RoomID
GROUP BY R.RoomType;

SELECT G.FirstName, G.LastName, COUNT(RES.ReservationID) AS NumberOfReservations
FROM Guests G
JOIN Reservations RES ON G.GuestID = RES.GuestID
GROUP BY G.GuestID, G.FirstName, G.LastName
HAVING COUNT(RES.ReservationID) > 3;

INSERT INTO Reservations (RoomID, GuestID, CheckInDate, CheckOutDate, TotalPrice)
SELECT R.RoomID, G.GuestID, '2024-01-10', '2024-01-15', R.PricePerNight * 5
FROM Rooms R
JOIN Guests G ON G.GuestID = 1 -- Assuming GuestID 1 for the new reservation
WHERE R.RoomID = 101; -- Assuming RoomID 101 for the new reservation

UPDATE Reservations
SET CheckOutDate = '2023-12-20',
    TotalPrice = (SELECT R.PricePerNight * DATEDIFF('2023-12-20', CheckInDate)
                  FROM Rooms R
                  JOIN Reservations RES2 ON R.RoomID = RES2.RoomID
                  WHERE RES2.ReservationID = 1)
WHERE ReservationID = 1;

SELECT
  P.ProductName,
  CI.Quantity
FROM Customers AS C
JOIN Carts AS CT
  ON C.CustomerID = CT.CustomerID
JOIN CartItems AS CI
  ON CT.CartID = CI.CartID
JOIN Products AS P
  ON CI.ProductID = P.ProductID
WHERE
  C.FirstName = 'customer_A';

SELECT
  C.FirstName,
  C.LastName,
  SUM(CI.Quantity * P.Price) AS TotalCartValue
FROM Customers AS C
JOIN Carts AS CT
  ON C.CustomerID = CT.CustomerID
JOIN CartItems AS CI
  ON CT.CartID = CI.CartID
JOIN Products AS P
  ON CI.ProductID = P.ProductID
GROUP BY
  C.CustomerID,

JOIN CartItems AS CI

GROUP BY
  C.CustomerID,
  C.FirstName,
  C.LastName
HAVING
  SUM(CI.Quantity) > 5;

Schema: Courses(CourseID INT, CourseName VARCHAR(100), Instructor VARCHAR(100)), Modules(ModuleID INT, CourseID INT, ModuleName VARCHAR(100), OrderInCourse INT), Enrollments(EnrollmentID INT, UserID INT, CourseID INT, StartDate DATE, CompletionDate DATE), Progress(ProgressID INT, EnrollmentID INT, ModuleID INT, CompletionStatus VARCHAR(20), CompletionDate DATETIME).
Queries:
1. List all 'In Progress' modules for 'User A' in 'Introduction to SQL'.
2. Calculate the percentage of modules completed by each user in a specific course.
3. Find courses where all enrolled students have completed at least 50% of the modules.
4. Enroll a new user in a course and mark the first module as 'Completed'.
5. Update the 'CompletionStatus' of a module for a user.
text_nat:
INSERT INTO Enrollments (UserID, CourseID, StartDate) VALUES
(101, (SELECT CourseID FROM Courses WHERE CourseName = 'Introduction to SQL'), CURDATE());

INSERT INTO Progress (EnrollmentID, ModuleID, CompletionStatus, CompletionDate) VALUES
((SELECT EnrollmentID FROM Enrollments WHERE UserID = 101 AND CourseID = (SELECT CourseID FROM Courses WHERE CourseName = 'Introduction to SQL')),
 (SELECT ModuleID FROM Modules WHERE CourseID = (SELECT CourseID FROM Courses WHERE CourseName = 'Introduction to SQL') ORDER BY OrderInCourse LIMIT 1),
 'Completed', NOW());

UPDATE Progress
SET CompletionStatus = 'Completed', CompletionDate = NOW()
WHERE EnrollmentID = (SELECT EnrollmentID FROM Enrollments WHERE UserID = 101 AND CourseID = (SELECT CourseID FROM Courses WHERE CourseName = 'Introduction to SQL'))
  AND ModuleID = (SELECT ModuleID FROM Modules WHERE ModuleName = 'Data Types' AND CourseID = (SELECT CourseID FROM Courses WHERE CourseName = 'Introduction to SQL'));

SELECT
    M.ModuleName
FROM
    Progress P
JOIN
    Enrollments E ON P.EnrollmentID = E.EnrollmentID
JOIN
    Courses C ON E.CourseID = C.CourseID
JOIN
    Modules M ON P.ModuleID = M.ModuleID
WHERE
    E.UserID = 101 AND C.CourseName = 'Introduction to SQL' AND P.CompletionStatus = 'In Progress';

SELECT
    E.UserID,
    C.CourseName,
    (COUNT(CASE WHEN P.CompletionStatus = 'Completed' THEN P.ModuleID END) * 100.0 / COUNT(M.ModuleID)) AS CompletionPercentage
FROM
    Enrollments E
JOIN
    Courses C ON E.CourseID = C.CourseID
JOIN
    Modules M ON C.CourseID = M.CourseID
LEFT JOIN
    Progress P ON E.EnrollmentID = P.EnrollmentID AND M.ModuleID = P.ModuleID
WHERE
    C.CourseName = 'Introduction to SQL'
GROUP BY
    E.UserID, C.CourseName;

SELECT
    C.CourseName
FROM
    Courses C
JOIN
    Enrollments E ON C.CourseID = E.CourseID
GROUP BY
    C.CourseID, C.CourseName
HAVING
    MIN((SELECT COUNT(P.ModuleID) FROM Progress P JOIN Modules M ON P.ModuleID = M.ModuleID WHERE P.EnrollmentID = E.EnrollmentID AND P.CompletionStatus = 'Completed') * 100.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Modules WHERE CourseID = C.CourseID)) >= 50;

HAVING

text_es: Schema: Documents (doc_id, title, latest_version_id), Versions (version_id, doc_id, version_number, content, created_at, created_by). Queries: 1. Retrieve the latest content for a specific document. 2. Find all versions of a document, ordered by version number. 3. Insert a new version for an existing document, updating the latest_version_id in Documents. 4. Find all documents created by a specific user. 5. Get the count of versions for each document.
text_nat:
-- 1. Retrieve the latest content for a specific document (e.g., doc_id = 1)
SELECT V.content
FROM Documents D
JOIN Versions V ON D.latest_version_id = V.version_id
WHERE D.doc_id = 1;

-- 2. Find all versions of a document, ordered by version number (e.g., doc_id = 1)
SELECT V.version_number, V.content, V.created_at, V.created_by
FROM Versions V
JOIN Documents D ON V.doc_id = D.doc_id
WHERE V.doc_id = 1
ORDER BY V.version_number;

-- 3. Insert a new version for an existing document, updating the latest_version_id
-- (Assuming doc_id = 1, new version_number = 3, content = 'New content', created_by = 'UserA')
INSERT INTO Versions (doc_id, version_number, content, created_at, created_by)
VALUES (1, 3, 'New content', NOW(), 'UserA');

UPDATE Documents
SET latest_version_id = (SELECT version_id FROM Versions WHERE doc_id = 1 AND version_number = 3)
WHERE doc_id = 1;

-- 4. Find all documents created by a specific user (e.g., 'UserA')
SELECT DISTINCT D.title
FROM Documents D
JOIN Versions V ON D.doc_id = V.doc_id
WHERE V.created_by = 'UserA';

-- 5. Get the count of versions for each document
SELECT D.title, COUNT(V.version_id) AS version_count
FROM Documents D
LEFT JOIN Versions V ON D.doc_id = V.doc_id
GROUP BY D.title
ORDER BY D.title;
text_alt:
-- 1. Retrieve the latest content for a specific document (e.g., doc_id = 1)
SELECT V.content
FROM Documents D, Versions V
WHERE D.latest_version_id = V.version_id
AND D.doc_id = 1;

-- 2. Find all versions of a document, ordered by version number (e.g., doc_id = 1)
SELECT V.version_number, V.content, V.created_at, V.created_by
FROM Versions V, Documents D
WHERE V.doc_id = D.doc_id
AND V.doc_id = 1
ORDER BY V.version_number;

-- 3. Insert a new version for an existing document, updating the latest_version_id
-- (Assuming doc_id = 1, new version_number = 3, content = 'New content', created_by = 'UserA')
INSERT INTO Versions (doc_id, version_number, content, created_at, created_by)
VALUES (1, 3, 'New content', NOW(), 'UserA');

UPDATE Documents
SET latest_version_id = (SELECT version_id FROM Versions WHERE doc_id = 1 AND version_number = 3)
WHERE doc_id = 1;

-- 4. Find all documents created by a specific user (e.g., 'UserA')
SELECT DISTINCT D.title
FROM Documents D, Versions V
WHERE D.doc_id = V.doc_id
AND V.created_by = 'UserA';

-- 5. Get the count of versions for each document
SELECT D.title, COUNT(V.version_id) AS version_count
FROM Documents D LEFT JOIN Versions V ON D.doc_id = V.doc_id
GROUP BY D.title
ORDER BY D.title;

text_es: Schema: Rooms (room_id, room_name, capacity), Bookings (booking_id, room_id, user_id, start_time, end_time, purpose). Queries: 1. Find all available rooms for a specific time slot. 2. List all bookings made by a particular user. 3. Insert a new meeting room booking. 4. Update the purpose of an existing booking. 5. Get the total number of bookings per room.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all available rooms for a specific time slot
SELECT r.room_id, r.room_name
FROM Rooms r
LEFT JOIN Bookings b ON r.room_id = b.room_id
AND (
    ('2024-07-20 10:00:00' < b.end_time AND '2024-07-20 11:00:00' > b.start_time)
)
WHERE b.booking_id IS NULL;

-- 2. List all bookings made by a particular user
SELECT b.booking_id, r.room_name, b.start_time, b.end_time, b.purpose
FROM Bookings b
JOIN Rooms r ON b.room_id = r.room_id
WHERE b.user_id = 1;

-- 3. Insert a new meeting room booking
INSERT INTO Bookings (room_id, user_id, start_time, end_time, purpose)
SELECT r.room_id, 2, '2024-07-21 14:00:00', '2024-07-21 15:00:00', 'Project Sync'
FROM Rooms r
WHERE r.room_name = 'Conference Room A';

-- 4. Update the purpose of an existing booking
UPDATE Bookings
SET purpose = 'Team Brainstorm'
WHERE booking_id = 1
AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM Rooms r
    JOIN Bookings b ON r.room_id = b.room_id
    WHERE b.booking_id = 1
);

-- 5. Get the total number of bookings per room
SELECT r.room_name, COUNT(b.booking_id) AS total_bookings
FROM Rooms r
LEFT JOIN Bookings b ON r.room_id = b.room_id
GROUP BY r.room_name
ORDER BY r.room_name;

text_es: Schema: Users (user_id, username, email), Subscriptions (sub_id, user_id, tier_id, start_date, end_date, is_active), Tiers (tier_id, tier_name, price_monthly). Queries: 1. Find the current active subscription tier for a user. 2. List all users on a specific subscription tier. 3. Update a user's subscription to a new tier (end current, start new). 4. Get the count of active users per tier. 5. Find all users whose subscriptions are expiring in the next 30 days.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find the current active subscription tier for a user (e.g., user_id = 1)
SELECT
    u.username,
    t.tier_name
FROM
    Users u
JOIN
    Subscriptions s ON u.user_id = s.user_id
JOIN
    Tiers t ON s.tier_id = t.tier_id
WHERE
    u.user_id = 1 AND s.is_active = TRUE;

-- 2. List all users on a specific subscription tier (e.g., 'Premium')
SELECT
    u.username,
    u.email
FROM
    Users u
JOIN
    Subscriptions s ON u.user_id = s.user_id
JOIN
    Tiers t ON s.tier_id = t.tier_id
WHERE
    t.tier_name = 'Premium' AND s.is_active = TRUE;

-- 3. Update a user's subscription to a new tier (e.g., user_id = 1, new tier_id = 3)
UPDATE Subscriptions SET is_active = FALSE, end_date = CURRENT_DATE WHERE user_id = 1 AND is_active = TRUE;
INSERT INTO Subscriptions (user_id, tier_id, start_date, end_date, is_active)
VALUES (1, 3, CURRENT_DATE, NULL, TRUE);

-- 4. Get the count of active users per tier
SELECT
    t.tier_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT u.user_id) AS active_users_count
FROM
    Users u
JOIN
    Subscriptions s ON u.user_id = s.user_id
JOIN
    Tiers t ON s.tier_id = t.tier_id
WHERE
    s.is_active = TRUE
GROUP BY
    t.tier_name;

-- 5. Find all users whose subscriptions are expiring in the next 30 days
SELECT
    u.username,
    u.email,
    s.end_date
FROM
    Users u
JOIN
    Subscriptions s ON u.user_id = s.user_id
WHERE
    s.is_active = TRUE AND s.end_date IS NOT NULL
    AND s.end_date BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE AND CURRENT_DATE + INTERVAL '30 days';

WHERE

INSERT INTO Subscriptions (user_id, tier_id, start_date, end_date, is_active)

Schema: Customers (customer_id, customer_name, email), Transactions (transaction_id, customer_id, amount, transaction_date), LoyaltyPoints (customer_id, points_balance, last_updated). Queries: 1. Get the current loyalty points for a customer. 2. Update a customer's loyalty points after a transaction (add points). 3. Find all customers with more than X points. 4. Get the total transaction amount for each customer. 5. List customers who haven't earned points in the last 90 days.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the current loyalty points for a customer.
SELECT
    lp.points_balance
FROM
    LoyaltyPoints lp
WHERE
    lp.customer_id = 1;

-- 2. Update a customer's loyalty points after a transaction (add points).
UPDATE LoyaltyPoints
SET points_balance = points_balance + 10
WHERE customer_id = 1;

-- 3. Find all customers with more than X points.
SELECT
    c.customer_name,
    lp.points_balance
FROM
    Customers c
JOIN
    LoyaltyPoints lp ON c.customer_id = lp.customer_id
WHERE
    lp.points_balance > 100;

-- 4. Get the total transaction amount for each customer.
SELECT
    c.customer_name,
    SUM(t.amount) AS total_amount_spent
FROM
    Customers c
JOIN
    Transactions t ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id
GROUP BY
    c.customer_name;

-- 5. List customers who haven't earned points in the last 90 days.
SELECT
    c.customer_name
FROM
    Customers c
LEFT JOIN
    LoyaltyPoints lp ON c.customer_id = lp.customer_id
WHERE
    lp.last_updated < DATE('now', '-90 days') OR lp.last_updated IS NULL;

-- 4. Get the total transaction amount for each customer.

FROM

WHERE
    c.customer_id = t.customer_id

-- 5. List customers who haven't earned points in the last 90 days.
SELECT

FROM
    Customers c,
    LoyaltyPoints lp
WHERE
    c.customer_id = lp.customer_id AND
    (lp.last_updated < DATE('now', '-90 days') OR lp.last_updated IS NULL);

text_es: Schema: Regions (region_id, region_name, manager_id), Salespeople (salesperson_id, region_id, salesperson_name), Sales (sale_id, salesperson_id, sale_amount, sale_date). Queries: 1. Find the total sales for a specific region. 2. List all salespeople in a given region. 3. Insert a new sale record. 4. Get the top 5 salespeople by total sales. 5. Find regions with sales below a certain target.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find the total sales for a specific region (e.g., 'North')
SELECT SUM(S.sale_amount) AS total_sales
FROM Sales S
JOIN Salespeople SP ON S.salesperson_id = SP.salesperson_id
JOIN Regions R ON SP.region_id = R.region_id
WHERE R.region_name = 'North';

-- 2. List all salespeople in a given region (e.g., 'East')
SELECT SP.salesperson_name
FROM Salespeople SP
JOIN Regions R ON SP.region_id = R.region_id
WHERE R.region_name = 'East';

-- 3. Insert a new sale record
INSERT INTO Sales (sale_id, salesperson_id, sale_amount, sale_date)
VALUES (101, 1, 1500.00, '2023-10-26');

-- 4. Get the top 5 salespeople by total sales
SELECT SP.salesperson_name, SUM(S.sale_amount) AS total_sales
FROM Sales S
JOIN Salespeople SP ON S.salesperson_id = SP.salesperson_id
GROUP BY SP.salesperson_name
ORDER BY total_sales DESC
LIMIT 5;

-- 5. Find regions with sales below a certain target (e.g., 10000)
SELECT R.region_name, SUM(S.sale_amount) AS region_total_sales
FROM Sales S
JOIN Salespeople SP ON S.salesperson_id = SP.salesperson_id
JOIN Regions R ON SP.region_id = R.region_id
GROUP BY R.region_name
HAVING SUM(S.sale_amount) < 10000;

text_nat:

FROM Podcasts AS P
JOIN Episodes AS E
  ON P.podcast_id = E.podcast_id

text_es: Schema: Products (product_id, product_name), Features (feature_id, product_id, feature_name, description), Requests (request_id, feature_id, user_id, requested_at, status). Queries: 1. Get all features for a specific product. 2. Find all requests for a particular feature. 3. Insert a new feature request. 4. Update the status of a feature request. 5. Count the number of requests per feature, ordered by popularity.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get all features for a specific product
SELECT
  f.feature_name,
  f.description
FROM Features AS f
JOIN Products AS p
  ON f.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE
  p.product_name = 'Example Product Name';

-- 2. Find all requests for a particular feature
SELECT
  r.request_id,
  r.user_id,
  r.requested_at,
  r.status
FROM Requests AS r
JOIN Features AS f
  ON r.feature_id = f.feature_id
WHERE
  f.feature_name = 'Example Feature Name';

-- 3. Insert a new feature request
INSERT INTO Requests (feature_id, user_id, requested_at, status)
SELECT
  f.feature_id,
  101,
  CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  'Pending'
FROM Features AS f
WHERE
  f.feature_name = 'Another Example Feature';

-- 4. Update the status of a feature request
UPDATE Requests
SET
  status = 'Completed'
FROM Requests AS r
JOIN Features AS f
  ON r.feature_id = f.feature_id
WHERE
  f.feature_name = 'Example Feature Name' AND r.user_id = 101 AND r.status = 'Pending';

-- 5. Count the number of requests per feature, ordered by popularity
SELECT
  f.feature_name,
  COUNT(r.request_id) AS request_count
FROM Features AS f
LEFT JOIN Requests AS r
  ON f.feature_id = r.feature_id
GROUP BY
  f.feature_name
ORDER BY
  request_count DESC;

text_es: Schema: Pages (page_id, page_url, page_title), Users (user_id, username), Views (view_id, page_id, user_id, view_timestamp). Queries: 1. Get the total number of views for a specific page. 2. List all pages viewed by a particular user. 3. Insert a new page view record. 4. Find the most viewed pages in the last 24 hours. 5. Count unique users who viewed each page.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the total number of views for a specific page.
SELECT COUNT(V.view_id) AS total_views
FROM Views V
JOIN Pages P ON V.page_id = P.page_id
WHERE P.page_url = 'https://example.com/some-page';

-- 2. List all pages viewed by a particular user.
SELECT DISTINCT P.page_title, P.page_url
FROM Views V
JOIN Pages P ON V.page_id = P.page_id
JOIN Users U ON V.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE U.username = 'john_doe';

-- 3. Insert a new page view record.
INSERT INTO Views (page_id, user_id, view_timestamp)
SELECT P.page_id, U.user_id, NOW()
FROM Pages P
JOIN Users U ON U.username = 'jane_doe'
WHERE P.page_url = 'https://example.com/another-page';

-- 4. Find the most viewed pages in the last 24 hours.
SELECT P.page_title, COUNT(V.view_id) AS view_count
FROM Views V
JOIN Pages P ON V.page_id = P.page_id
WHERE V.view_timestamp >= NOW() - INTERVAL '24 HOURS'
GROUP BY P.page_title
ORDER BY view_count DESC
LIMIT 5;

-- 5. Count unique users who viewed each page.
SELECT P.page_title, COUNT(DISTINCT U.user_id) AS unique_viewers
FROM Views V
JOIN Pages P ON V.page_id = P.page_id
JOIN Users U ON V.user_id = U.user_id
GROUP BY P.page_title
ORDER BY unique_viewers DESC;

text_es: Schema: Conferences (conference_id, conference_name, start_date), Speakers (speaker_id, speaker_name, bio, company), Sessions (session_id, conference_id, speaker_id, session_title, start_time, end_time). Queries: 1. List all sessions at a specific conference. 2. Find all sessions presented by a particular speaker. 3. Insert a new session for a conference with a speaker. 4. Update a speaker's bio. 5. Get the count of sessions per speaker.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all sessions at a specific conference.
SELECT
  s.session_title,
  s.start_time,
  s.end_time,
  c.conference_name
FROM Sessions AS s
JOIN Conferences AS c
  ON s.conference_id = c.conference_id
WHERE
  c.conference_name = 'Tech Summit 2024';

-- 2. Find all sessions presented by a particular speaker.
SELECT
  s.session_title,
  c.conference_name,
  s.start_time,
  s.end_time
FROM Sessions AS s
JOIN Speakers AS sp
  ON s.speaker_id = sp.speaker_id
JOIN Conferences AS c
  ON s.conference_id = c.conference_id
WHERE
  sp.speaker_name = 'Dr. Emily Carter';

-- 3. Insert a new session for a conference with a speaker.
INSERT INTO Sessions (conference_id, speaker_id, session_title, start_time, end_time)
SELECT
  c.conference_id,
  sp.speaker_id,
  'Advanced AI Techniques',
  '2024-11-15 14:00:00',
  '2024-11-15 15:00:00'
FROM Conferences AS c
JOIN Speakers AS sp
  ON 1 = 1 -- Dummy join condition, filtered by WHERE
WHERE
  c.conference_name = 'AI World Congress' AND sp.speaker_name = 'Dr. Emily Carter';

-- 4. Update a speaker's bio.
UPDATE Speakers
SET
  bio = 'Experienced AI researcher focusing on neural networks and machine learning.'
WHERE
  speaker_name = 'Dr. Emily Carter';

-- 5. Get the count of sessions per speaker.
SELECT
  sp.speaker_name,
  COUNT(s.session_id) AS session_count
FROM Speakers AS sp
LEFT JOIN Sessions AS s
  ON sp.speaker_id = s.speaker_id
GROUP BY
  sp.speaker_name
ORDER BY
  session_count DESC;

Queries: 1. Get the total number of likes for a specific post. 2. List all comments on a particular post. 3. Insert a new like for a post by a user. 4. Find posts with more than X comments. 5. Get the total engagement (likes + comments) for each post.

SELECT COUNT(l.like_id) AS total_likes
FROM Likes AS l
WHERE l.post_id = 1;

FROM Comments AS c

WHERE c.post_id = 1;

SELECT p.post_id, p.content
FROM Posts AS p
JOIN (
    SELECT post_id, COUNT(comment_id) AS comment_count
    FROM Comments
    GROUP BY post_id
    HAVING COUNT(comment_id) > 2
) AS pc ON p.post_id = pc.post_id;

SELECT p.post_id, p.content,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.like_id) AS total_likes,
       COUNT(DISTINCT c.comment_id) AS total_comments,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.like_id) + COUNT(DISTINCT c.comment_id) AS total_engagement
FROM Posts AS p
LEFT JOIN Likes AS l ON p.post_id = l.post_id
LEFT JOIN Comments AS c ON p.post_id = c.post_id
GROUP BY p.post_id, p.content
ORDER BY total_engagement DESC;

text_es: Schema: Vehicles (vehicle_id, make, model, year, license_plate), MaintenanceRecords (record_id, vehicle_id, service_type, service_date, cost, mileage_at_service). Queries: 1. Get all maintenance records for a specific vehicle. 2. Find the total maintenance cost for each vehicle. 3. Insert a new maintenance record. 4. Find vehicles that haven't had a specific service type in over a year. 5. List vehicles due for service based on mileage (e.g., last service at 50k, due every 10k, current mileage 59k).
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Vehicles (
    vehicle_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    make VARCHAR(50),
    model VARCHAR(50),
    year INT,
    license_plate VARCHAR(20)
);

CREATE TABLE MaintenanceRecords (
    record_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    vehicle_id INT,
    service_type VARCHAR(100),
    service_date DATE,
    cost DECIMAL(10, 2),
    mileage_at_service INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (vehicle_id) REFERENCES Vehicles(vehicle_id)
);

Get the highest score for a specific quiz by a user. 2. List all attempts for a quiz, ordered by score. 3. Insert a new quiz attempt with a score. 4. Find the average score for each quiz. 5. List users who have not attempted a specific quiz.
text_nat:
SELECT MAX(T1.score) AS highest_score
FROM Attempts AS T1
JOIN Quizzes AS T2 ON T1.quiz_id = T2.quiz_id
WHERE T2.quiz_title = 'Specific Quiz Title' AND T1.user_id = 1;

SELECT T1.attempt_id, T1.user_id, T1.score, T1.attempt_date
FROM Attempts AS T1
JOIN Quizzes AS T2 ON T1.quiz_id = T2.quiz_id

ORDER BY T1.score DESC;

JOIN Quizzes AS T2 ON T1.quiz_id = T2.quiz_id
GROUP BY T2.quiz_title;

SELECT u.user_id
FROM Users u
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT T1.user_id
    FROM Attempts AS T1
    JOIN Quizzes AS T2 ON T1.quiz_id = T2.quiz_id
    WHERE T2.quiz_title = 'Specific Quiz Title'

WHERE attempted_users.user_id IS NULL;

text_es: Schema: Bugs (bug_id, title, description, reporter_id, reported_date, status), Users (user_id, username), BugAssignments (assignment_id, bug_id, assigned_to_user_id, assigned_date, resolution_date). Queries: 1. Find all bugs assigned to a specific user. 2. List all open bugs. 3. Assign a bug to a user. 4. Update the status of a bug to 'resolved'. 5. Count bugs reported by each user.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all bugs assigned to a specific user
SELECT B.bug_id, B.title, B.description
FROM Bugs AS B
JOIN BugAssignments AS BA ON B.bug_id = BA.bug_id
WHERE BA.assigned_to_user_id = 1; -- Replace 1 with the specific user_id

-- 2. List all open bugs
SELECT bug_id, title, description, reported_date
FROM Bugs
WHERE status = 'open';

-- 3. Assign a bug to a user
INSERT INTO BugAssignments (bug_id, assigned_to_user_id, assigned_date)
VALUES (101, 2, CURRENT_DATE); -- Replace 101 with bug_id and 2 with user_id

-- 4. Update the status of a bug to 'resolved'
UPDATE Bugs
SET status = 'resolved'
WHERE bug_id = 101; -- Replace 101 with the bug_id

-- 5. Count bugs reported by each user
SELECT U.username, COUNT(B.bug_id) AS reported_bug_count
FROM Users AS U
LEFT JOIN Bugs AS B ON U.user_id = B.reporter_id
GROUP BY U.username
ORDER BY reported_bug_count DESC;

text_es: Schema: Products (product_id, product_name), Prices (price_id, product_id, effective_date, price_usd). Queries: 1. Get the current price for a specific product. 2. List the full pricing history for a product. 3. Insert a new price for a product (new effective date). 4. Find products whose price has increased in the last year. 5. Get the latest price for all products.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Products (
    product_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Prices (
    price_id INT PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,
    product_id INT,
    effective_date DATE,
    price_usd DECIMAL(10, 2),
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES Products(product_id)
);

-- 1. Get the current price for a specific product
SELECT p.product_name, pr.price_usd
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE p.product_id = 1 AND pr.effective_date = (
    SELECT MAX(effective_date)
    FROM Prices
    WHERE product_id = p.product_id
);

-- 2. List the full pricing history for a product
SELECT p.product_name, pr.effective_date, pr.price_usd
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE p.product_id = 1
ORDER BY pr.effective_date DESC;

-- 3. Insert a new price for a product (new effective date)
INSERT INTO Prices (product_id, effective_date, price_usd)
VALUES (1, '2023-11-01', 25.00);

-- 4. Find products whose price has increased in the last year
SELECT p.product_name
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr1 ON p.product_id = pr1.product_id
JOIN Prices pr2 ON p.product_id = pr2.product_id
WHERE pr1.effective_date = (SELECT MAX(effective_date) FROM Prices WHERE product_id = p.product_id AND effective_date >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR))
  AND pr2.effective_date = (SELECT MAX(effective_date) FROM Prices WHERE product_id = p.product_id AND effective_date < (SELECT MAX(effective_date) FROM Prices WHERE product_id = p.product_id AND effective_date >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR)))
  AND pr1.price_usd > pr2.price_usd;

-- 5. Get the latest price for all products
SELECT p.product_name, sub.price_usd
FROM Products p
JOIN (
    SELECT product_id, price_usd, effective_date
    FROM Prices
    WHERE (product_id, effective_date) IN (
        SELECT product_id, MAX(effective_date)
        FROM Prices
        GROUP BY product_id
    )
) AS sub ON p.product_id = sub.product_id;

text_es: Schema: Departments (dept_id, dept_name, budget_total), Expenses (expense_id, dept_id, expense_date, amount, description). Queries: 1. Get the total expenses for a specific department. 2. List all expenses for a department in a given month. 3. Insert a new expense record. 4. Find departments that are over budget. 5. Get the remaining budget for each department.
text_nat:
-- 1. Total expenses for a specific department
SELECT SUM(e.amount) AS total_expenses
FROM Expenses e
JOIN Departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id
WHERE d.dept_name = 'Sales';

-- 2. List all expenses for a department in a given month
SELECT e.expense_date, e.amount, e.description
FROM Expenses e
JOIN Departments d ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id
WHERE d.dept_name = 'Marketing' AND STRFTIME('%Y-%m', e.expense_date) = '2023-10';

-- 3. Insert a new expense record
INSERT INTO Expenses (dept_id, expense_date, amount, description)
SELECT d.dept_id, '2023-11-15', 500.00, 'Office Supplies'
FROM Departments d
WHERE d.dept_name = 'HR';

-- 4. Find departments that are over budget
SELECT d.dept_name, d.budget_total, SUM(e.amount) AS total_spent
FROM Departments d
JOIN Expenses e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id
GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name, d.budget_total
HAVING SUM(e.amount) > d.budget_total;

-- 5. Get the remaining budget for each department
SELECT d.dept_name, d.budget_total - COALESCE(SUM(e.amount), 0) AS remaining_budget
FROM Departments d
LEFT JOIN Expenses e ON d.dept_id = e.dept_id
GROUP BY d.dept_id, d.dept_name, d.budget_total;

text_es: Schema: Agents (agent_id, agent_name, department), Tickets (ticket_id, agent_id, customer_id, opened_at, closed_at, status, resolution_notes). Queries: 1. Get the number of tickets closed by a specific agent. 2. List all open tickets assigned to an agent. 3. Assign a ticket to an agent. 4. Close a ticket with resolution notes. 5. Find agents with an average resolution time longer than X hours.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the number of tickets closed by a specific agent.
SELECT COUNT(T.ticket_id)
FROM Tickets AS T
JOIN Agents AS A ON T.agent_id = A.agent_id
WHERE A.agent_name = 'Alice Smith' AND T.status = 'Closed';

-- 2. List all open tickets assigned to an agent.
SELECT T.ticket_id, T.opened_at
FROM Tickets AS T
JOIN Agents AS A ON T.agent_id = A.agent_id
WHERE A.agent_name = 'Bob Johnson' AND T.status = 'Open';

-- 3. Assign a ticket to an agent.
UPDATE Tickets
SET agent_id = (SELECT A.agent_id FROM Agents AS A WHERE A.agent_name = 'Charlie Brown')
WHERE ticket_id = 101 AND status = 'Open';

-- 4. Close a ticket with resolution notes.
UPDATE Tickets
SET status = 'Closed', closed_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, resolution_notes = 'Issue resolved after troubleshooting.'
WHERE ticket_id = 102;

-- 5. Find agents with an average resolution time longer than X hours (e.g., 24 hours).
SELECT A.agent_name, AVG(JULIANDAY(T.closed_at) - JULIANDAY(T.opened_at)) * 24 AS average_resolution_hours
FROM Agents AS A
JOIN Tickets AS T ON A.agent_id = T.agent_id
WHERE T.status = 'Closed'
GROUP BY A.agent_name
HAVING average_resolution_hours > 24;

text_es: Schema: Projects (project_id, project_name, start_date, end_date), Tasks (task_id, project_id, task_name, due_date, status), TaskDependencies (task_id, depends_on_task_id). Queries: 1. List all tasks for a specific project. 2. Find all tasks that a specific task depends on. 3. Insert a new task dependency. 4. Find tasks that are 'pending' but have all their dependencies 'completed'. 5. Get the count of dependencies for each task.
text_nat:
SELECT task_name, due_date, status
FROM Tasks
JOIN Projects ON Tasks.project_id = Projects.project_id
WHERE Projects.project_name = 'Alpha Project';

SELECT T2.task_name AS dependency_name
FROM TaskDependencies TD
JOIN Tasks T1 ON TD.task_id = T1.task_id
JOIN Tasks T2 ON TD.depends_on_task_id = T2.task_id
WHERE T1.task_name = 'Develop UI';

INSERT INTO TaskDependencies (task_id, depends_on_task_id)
VALUES (
    (SELECT task_id FROM Tasks WHERE task_name = 'Test Backend'),
    (SELECT task_id FROM Tasks WHERE task_name = 'Implement API')
);

SELECT T.task_name
FROM Tasks T
LEFT JOIN TaskDependencies TD ON T.task_id = TD.task_id
LEFT JOIN Tasks DPT ON TD.depends_on_task_id = DPT.task_id
WHERE T.status = 'pending'
GROUP BY T.task_id, T.task_name
HAVING COUNT(TD.depends_on_task_id) = SUM(CASE WHEN DPT.status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END);

SELECT T.task_name, COUNT(TD.depends_on_task_id) AS dependency_count
FROM Tasks T
LEFT JOIN TaskDependencies TD ON T.task_id = TD.task_id
GROUP BY T.task_id, T.task_name;

WHERE Tasks.project_id = Projects.project_id

FROM TaskDependencies TD, Tasks T1, Tasks T2
WHERE TD.task_id = T1.task_id
AND TD.depends_on_task_id = T2.task_id
AND T1.task_name = 'Develop UI';

FROM Tasks T

GROUP BY T.task_id, T.task_name;

text_es: Schema: Courses (course_id, course_title), Modules (module_id, course_id, module_title, order_index), Lessons (lesson_id, module_id, lesson_title, lesson_type, duration_minutes). Queries: 1. List all modules for a specific course, ordered. 2. Find all lessons within a particular module. 3. Insert a new lesson into a module. 4. Update the order index of a module. 5. Get the total duration of lessons per module.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all modules for a specific course, ordered.
SELECT M.module_title, M.order_index
FROM Modules AS M
JOIN Courses AS C ON M.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE C.course_title = 'Data Science Fundamentals'
ORDER BY M.order_index;

-- 2. Find all lessons within a particular module.
SELECT L.lesson_title, L.lesson_type, L.duration_minutes
FROM Lessons AS L
JOIN Modules AS M ON L.module_id = M.module_id
WHERE M.module_title = 'Introduction to Python';

-- 3. Insert a new lesson into a module.
INSERT INTO Lessons (module_id, lesson_title, lesson_type, duration_minutes)
SELECT M.module_id, 'New Lesson Title', 'Video', 15
FROM Modules AS M
JOIN Courses AS C ON M.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE M.module_title = 'SQL Basics' AND C.course_title = 'Data Science Fundamentals';

-- 4. Update the order index of a module.
UPDATE Modules
SET order_index = 3
FROM Modules AS M
JOIN Courses AS C ON M.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE M.module_title = 'Advanced Algorithms' AND C.course_title = 'Computer Science I';

-- 5. Get the total duration of lessons per module.
SELECT M.module_title, SUM(L.duration_minutes) AS total_duration
FROM Modules AS M
LEFT JOIN Lessons AS L ON M.module_id = L.module_id
GROUP BY M.module_title
ORDER BY total_duration DESC;

text_es: Schema: Events (event_id, event_name, event_date), Attendees (attendee_id, event_id, first_name, last_name, company, badge_printed). Queries: 1. List all attendees for a specific event. 2. Find all attendees from a particular company for an event. 3. Mark an attendee's badge as 'printed'. 4. Insert a new attendee for an event. 5. Get the count of attendees whose badges have not been printed.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all attendees for a specific event
SELECT
  a.first_name,
  a.last_name,
  a.company
FROM Attendees AS a
JOIN Events AS e
  ON a.event_id = e.event_id
WHERE
  e.event_name = 'Tech Conference 2023';

-- 2. Find all attendees from a particular company for an event
SELECT
  a.first_name,
  a.last_name
FROM Attendees AS a
JOIN Events AS e
  ON a.event_id = e.event_id
WHERE
  e.event_name = 'Tech Conference 2023' AND a.company = 'Innovate Corp';

-- 3. Mark an attendee's badge as 'printed'
UPDATE Attendees
SET
  badge_printed = TRUE
WHERE
  attendee_id = 101;

-- 4. Insert a new attendee for an event
INSERT INTO Attendees (event_id, first_name, last_name, company, badge_printed)
SELECT
  e.event_id,
  'Jane',
  'Doe',
  'Global Solutions',
  FALSE
FROM Events AS e
WHERE
  e.event_name = 'Data Science Summit 2024';

-- 5. Get the count of attendees whose badges have not been printed
SELECT
  COUNT(a.attendee_id) AS unprinted_badge_count
FROM Attendees AS a
JOIN Events AS e
  ON a.event_id = e.event_id
WHERE
  a.badge_printed = FALSE AND e.event_name = 'Tech Conference 2023';

text_es: Schema: Users (user_id, username, email), NotificationTypes (type_id, type_name, description), UserPreferences (user_id, type_id, enabled). Queries: 1. Get all notification preferences for a specific user. 2. Find all users who have a specific notification type enabled. 3. Update a user's preference for a notification type. 4. Find all notification types that are enabled by default (i.e., not in UserPreferences with enabled=false). 5. Count users who have opted out of a specific notification type.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get all notification preferences for a specific user
SELECT
  U.username,
  NT.type_name,
  UP.enabled
FROM Users AS U
JOIN UserPreferences AS UP
  ON U.user_id = UP.user_id
JOIN NotificationTypes AS NT
  ON UP.type_id = NT.type_id
WHERE
  U.username = 'some_username';

-- 2. Find all users who have a specific notification type enabled
SELECT
  U.username,
  U.email
FROM Users AS U
JOIN UserPreferences AS UP
  ON U.user_id = UP.user_id
JOIN NotificationTypes AS NT
  ON UP.type_id = NT.type_id
WHERE
  NT.type_name = 'Email Notifications' AND UP.enabled = TRUE;

-- 3. Update a user's preference for a notification type
UPDATE UserPreferences
SET
  enabled = FALSE
FROM Users AS U
JOIN NotificationTypes AS NT
  ON UserPreferences.type_id = NT.type_id
WHERE
  UserPreferences.user_id = U.user_id AND U.username = 'another_user' AND NT.type_name = 'SMS Alerts';

-- 4. Find all notification types that are enabled by default
SELECT
  NT.type_name,
  NT.description
FROM NotificationTypes AS NT
LEFT JOIN UserPreferences AS UP
  ON NT.type_id = UP.type_id AND UP.enabled = FALSE
WHERE
  UP.user_id IS NULL;

-- 5. Count users who have opted out of a specific notification type
SELECT
  COUNT(U.user_id)
FROM Users AS U
JOIN UserPreferences AS UP
  ON U.user_id = UP.user_id
JOIN NotificationTypes AS NT
  ON UP.type_id = NT.type_id
WHERE
  NT.type_name = 'Promotional Offers' AND UP.enabled = FALSE;

text_es: Schema: Assets (asset_id, asset_tag, asset_type, purchase_date, cost), Locations (location_id, location_name), AssetLocations (asset_id, location_id, assigned_date, released_date). Queries: 1. Get the current location of a specific asset. 2. List all assets at a particular location. 3. Assign an asset to a new location (end old assignment, start new). 4. Find assets purchased before a specific date. 5. Get the total cost of assets per asset type.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the current location of a specific asset (asset_id = 1)
SELECT
    A.asset_id,
    A.asset_tag,
    L.location_name
FROM
    Assets AS A
JOIN
    AssetLocations AS AL ON A.asset_id = AL.asset_id
JOIN
    Locations AS L ON AL.location_id = L.location_id
WHERE
    A.asset_id = 1 AND AL.released_date IS NULL;

-- 2. List all assets at a particular location (location_id = 1)
SELECT
    A.asset_id,
    A.asset_tag,
    A.asset_type
FROM
    Assets AS A
JOIN
    AssetLocations AS AL ON A.asset_id = AL.asset_id
WHERE
    AL.location_id = 1 AND AL.released_date IS NULL;

-- 3. Assign an asset to a new location (asset_id = 2, new_location_id = 3)
UPDATE AssetLocations
SET released_date = CURRENT_DATE
WHERE asset_id = 2 AND released_date IS NULL;

INSERT INTO AssetLocations (asset_id, location_id, assigned_date, released_date)
VALUES (2, 3, CURRENT_DATE, NULL);

-- 4. Find assets purchased before a specific date ('2023-01-01')
SELECT
    A.asset_id,
    A.asset_tag,
    A.purchase_date,
    A.cost
FROM
    Assets AS A
WHERE
    A.purchase_date < '2023-01-01';

-- 5. Get the total cost of assets per asset type
SELECT
    A.asset_type,
    SUM(A.cost) AS total_cost
FROM
    Assets AS A
GROUP BY
    A.asset_type;

text_es: Schema: Posts (post_id, content, user_id, posted_at), Reactions (reaction_id, post_id, user_id, reaction_type, reacted_at). Queries: 1. Get the total count of a specific reaction type for a post. 2. List all users who reacted to a particular post. 3. Insert a new reaction to a post. 4. Find posts with more than 10 'like' reactions. 5. Get the total number of unique users who reacted to each post.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the total count of a specific reaction type for a post.
SELECT COUNT(R.reaction_id)
FROM Reactions AS R
WHERE R.post_id = 1 AND R.reaction_type = 'like';

-- 2. List all users who reacted to a particular post.
SELECT DISTINCT U.user_id, U.username -- Assuming a Users table exists for username. If not, just U.user_id.
FROM Reactions AS R
JOIN Users AS U ON R.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE R.post_id = 1;

-- 3. Insert a new reaction to a post.
INSERT INTO Reactions (post_id, user_id, reaction_type, reacted_at)
VALUES (1, 2, 'love', NOW());

-- 4. Find posts with more than 10 'like' reactions.
SELECT P.post_id, P.content
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Reactions AS R ON P.post_id = R.post_id
WHERE R.reaction_type = 'like'
GROUP BY P.post_id, P.content
HAVING COUNT(R.reaction_id) > 10;

-- 5. Get the total number of unique users who reacted to each post.
SELECT P.post_id, P.content, COUNT(DISTINCT R.user_id) AS unique_reacting_users
FROM Posts AS P
LEFT JOIN Reactions AS R ON P.post_id = R.post_id
GROUP BY P.post_id, P.content;

text_es: Schema: Products (product_id, product_name, price), Customers (customer_id, customer_name), Returns (return_id, customer_id, product_id, return_date, reason, refund_amount). Queries: 1. List all returns made by a specific customer. 2. Find all returns for a particular product. 3. Insert a new product return record. 4. Get the total refund amount for each customer. 5. Find products with more than 10 returns in the last month.
text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM Returns
JOIN Customers ON Returns.customer_id = Customers.customer_id
WHERE Customers.customer_name = 'John Doe';

SELECT R.*, P.product_name
FROM Returns AS R
JOIN Products AS P ON R.product_id = P.product_id
WHERE P.product_name = 'Laptop';

    C.customer_name,
    SUM(R.refund_amount) AS total_refund_amount
FROM Customers AS C
JOIN Returns AS R ON C.customer_id = R.customer_id
GROUP BY C.customer_name;

SELECT
    P.product_name,
    COUNT(R.return_id) AS total_returns
FROM Products AS P
JOIN Returns AS R ON P.product_id = R.product_id
WHERE R.return_date >= DATE('now', '-1 month')
GROUP BY P.product_name
HAVING COUNT(R.return_id) > 10;

text_es: Schema: Customers (customer_id, customer_name, email), Segments (segment_id, segment_name, description), CustomerSegments (customer_id, segment_id, assigned_date). Queries: 1. List all segments a specific customer belongs to. 2. Find all customers in a particular segment. 3. Assign a customer to a new segment. 4. Get the count of customers per segment. 5. Find customers who are not assigned to any segment.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all segments a specific customer belongs to.
SELECT
  s.segment_name,
  s.description
FROM Customers AS c
JOIN CustomerSegments AS cs
  ON c.customer_id = cs.customer_id
JOIN Segments AS s
  ON cs.segment_id = s.segment_id
WHERE
  c.customer_name = 'John Doe';

-- 2. Find all customers in a particular segment.
SELECT
  c.customer_name,
  c.email
FROM Segments AS s
JOIN CustomerSegments AS cs
  ON s.segment_id = cs.segment_id
JOIN Customers AS c
  ON cs.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE
  s.segment_name = 'Premium';

-- 3. Assign a customer to a new segment.
INSERT INTO CustomerSegments (customer_id, segment_id, assigned_date)
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  s.segment_id,
  CURRENT_DATE
FROM Customers AS c
JOIN Segments AS s
  ON s.segment_name = 'New Arrivals'
WHERE
  c.customer_name = 'Jane Smith';

-- 4. Get the count of customers per segment.
SELECT
  s.segment_name,
  COUNT(cs.customer_id) AS customer_count
FROM Segments AS s
LEFT JOIN CustomerSegments AS cs
  ON s.segment_id = cs.segment_id
GROUP BY
  s.segment_name;

-- 5. Find customers who are not assigned to any segment.
SELECT
  c.customer_name,
  c.email
FROM Customers AS c
LEFT JOIN CustomerSegments AS cs
  ON c.customer_id = cs.customer_id
WHERE
  cs.segment_id IS NULL;

List all events performed by a specific user. 2. Find the total occurrences of a particular event. 3. Insert a new user event. 4. Get the top 5 most frequent events. 5. Count unique users who performed each event.
text_nat:
SELECT E.event_name, E.description
FROM Events AS E
JOIN UserEvents AS UE ON E.event_id = UE.event_id
JOIN Users AS U ON UE.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE U.username = 'specific_user_name';

SELECT COUNT(UE.event_id) AS total_occurrences
FROM UserEvents AS UE
JOIN Events AS E ON UE.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE E.event_name = 'particular_event_name';

SELECT U.user_id, E.event_id, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, '{"key": "value"}'
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Events AS E ON E.event_name = 'New Event'
WHERE U.username = 'new_user';

SELECT E.event_name, COUNT(UE.event_id) AS event_count
FROM Events AS E
JOIN UserEvents AS UE ON E.event_id = UE.event_id
GROUP BY E.event_name
ORDER BY event_count DESC
LIMIT 5;

SELECT E.event_name, COUNT(DISTINCT U.user_id) AS unique_user_count
FROM Events AS E
JOIN UserEvents AS UE ON E.event_id = UE.event_id
JOIN Users AS U ON UE.user_id = U.user_id
GROUP BY E.event_name;

FROM Events AS E, UserEvents AS UE, Users AS U
WHERE E.event_id = UE.event_id AND UE.user_id = U.user_id

FROM UserEvents AS UE, Events AS E

GROUP BY E.event_name
ORDER BY event_count DESC

WHERE E.event_id = UE.event_id AND UE.user_id = U.user_id

text_es: Schema: Departments (dept_id, dept_name), Staff (staff_id, staff_name, dept_id, role, hire_date). Queries: 1. List all staff in a specific department. 2. Find all staff with a particular role. 3. Insert a new staff member into a department. 4. Update a staff member's role. 5. Get the count of staff members per role in each department.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Departments (
    dept_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    dept_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Staff (
    staff_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    staff_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    dept_id INT,
    role VARCHAR(50),
    hire_date DATE,
    FOREIGN KEY (dept_id) REFERENCES Departments(dept_id)
);

-- 2. Find all staff with a particular role (e.g., 'Engineer')

text_es: Schema: Projects (project_id, project_name, total_budget), Categories (category_id, category_name), BudgetAllocations (allocation_id, project_id, category_id, allocated_amount, spent_amount). Queries: 1. Get the total allocated amount for a specific project. 2. List all budget allocations for a project, by category. 3. Update the spent amount for a specific allocation. 4. Find projects that have exceeded their budget in any category. 5. Calculate remaining budget per project (total_budget - sum(spent_amount)).
text_nat:
SELECT SUM(ba.allocated_amount) AS total_allocated_amount
FROM BudgetAllocations ba
JOIN Projects p ON ba.project_id = p.project_id
WHERE p.project_name = 'Alpha Project';

SELECT p.project_name, c.category_name, ba.allocated_amount, ba.spent_amount
FROM BudgetAllocations ba
JOIN Projects p ON ba.project_id = p.project_id
JOIN Categories c ON ba.category_id = c.category_id
WHERE p.project_name = 'Alpha Project'
ORDER BY c.category_name;

UPDATE BudgetAllocations
SET spent_amount = 1500
WHERE allocation_id = 1;

SELECT DISTINCT p.project_name
FROM Projects p
JOIN BudgetAllocations ba ON p.project_id = ba.project_id
WHERE ba.spent_amount > ba.allocated_amount;

SELECT p.project_name,
       p.total_budget - COALESCE(SUM(ba.spent_amount), 0) AS remaining_budget
FROM Projects p
LEFT JOIN BudgetAllocations ba ON p.project_id = ba.project_id
GROUP BY p.project_id, p.total_budget
ORDER BY p.project_name;

text_es: Schema: Providers (provider_id, provider_name, specialty), Certifications (cert_id, cert_name, issuing_body), ProviderCertifications (provider_id, cert_id, issue_date, expiry_date). Queries: 1. List all certifications held by a specific provider. 2. Find all providers with a particular certification. 3. Insert a new certification for a provider. 4. Find providers whose certifications are expiring in the next 90 days. 5. Get the count of providers per specialty.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all certifications held by a specific provider.
SELECT
    P.provider_name,
    C.cert_name,
    PC.issue_date,
    PC.expiry_date
FROM Providers P
JOIN ProviderCertifications PC ON P.provider_id = PC.provider_id
JOIN Certifications C ON PC.cert_id = C.cert_id
WHERE P.provider_name = 'Dr. Alice Smith';

-- 2. Find all providers with a particular certification.
SELECT
    P.provider_name,
    P.specialty
FROM Providers P
JOIN ProviderCertifications PC ON P.provider_id = PC.provider_id
JOIN Certifications C ON PC.cert_id = C.cert_id
WHERE C.cert_name = 'Advanced Cardiac Life Support';

-- 3. Insert a new certification for a provider.
INSERT INTO ProviderCertifications (provider_id, cert_id, issue_date, expiry_date)
SELECT
    P.provider_id,
    C.cert_id,
    '2023-01-01',
    '2025-01-01'
FROM Providers P
JOIN Certifications C ON C.cert_name = 'Pediatric Advanced Life Support'
WHERE P.provider_name = 'Dr. Bob Johnson';

-- 4. Find providers whose certifications are expiring in the next 90 days.
SELECT
    P.provider_name,
    C.cert_name,
    PC.expiry_date
FROM Providers P
JOIN ProviderCertifications PC ON P.provider_id = PC.provider_id
JOIN Certifications C ON PC.cert_id = C.cert_id
WHERE PC.expiry_date BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE AND DATE('now', '+90 days');

-- 5. Get the count of providers per specialty.
SELECT
    P.specialty,
    COUNT(P.provider_id) AS provider_count
FROM Providers P
GROUP BY P.specialty;

text_es: Schema: Users (user_id, username), Products (product_id, product_name, price), Wishlists (wishlist_id, user_id, product_id, added_date, quantity). Queries: 1. List all products in a specific user's wishlist. 2. Find all users who have a particular product in their wishlist. 3. Add a product to a user's wishlist. 4. Remove a product from a user's wishlist. 5. Get the total number of products in wishlists across all users.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all products in a specific user's wishlist (e.g., user_id = 1)
SELECT
    P.product_name,
    P.price,
    W.quantity
FROM
    Wishlists W
JOIN
    Products P ON W.product_id = P.product_id
WHERE
    W.user_id = 1;

-- 2. Find all users who have a particular product in their wishlist (e.g., product_id = 101)
SELECT
    U.username
FROM
    Users U
JOIN
    Wishlists W ON U.user_id = W.user_id
WHERE
    W.product_id = 101;

-- 3. Add a product to a user's wishlist (e.g., user_id = 2, product_id = 103, quantity = 1)
INSERT INTO Wishlists (user_id, product_id, added_date, quantity)
VALUES (2, 103, CURRENT_DATE, 1);

-- 4. Remove a product from a user's wishlist (e.g., user_id = 1, product_id = 102)
DELETE FROM Wishlists
WHERE user_id = 1 AND product_id = 102;

-- 5. Get the total number of products in wishlists across all users
SELECT
    SUM(W.quantity) AS total_products_in_wishlists
FROM
    Wishlists W
JOIN
    Users U ON W.user_id = U.user_id; -- Example of JOIN for consistency, though not strictly needed for SUM(quantity)

text_es: Schema: Subscriptions (sub_id, user_id, plan_id, start_date, end_date), Plans (plan_id, plan_name, monthly_cost, data_limit_gb), UsageRecords (usage_id, sub_id, usage_date, data_used_gb). Queries: 1. Get the total data used by a specific subscription in a month. 2. List all subscriptions on a particular plan. 3. Record new data usage for a subscription. 4. Find subscriptions that have exceeded their data limit. 5. Calculate the remaining data limit for each active subscription.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the total data used by a specific subscription in a month.
SELECT
    SUM(ur.data_used_gb) AS total_data_used
FROM
    UsageRecords ur
JOIN
    Subscriptions s ON ur.sub_id = s.sub_id
WHERE
    ur.sub_id = 101 AND STRFTIME('%Y-%m', ur.usage_date) = '2023-10';

-- 2. List all subscriptions on a particular plan.
SELECT
    s.sub_id,
    s.user_id,
    s.start_date,
    s.end_date
FROM
    Subscriptions s
JOIN
    Plans p ON s.plan_id = p.plan_id
WHERE
    p.plan_name = 'Premium Plan';

-- 3. Record new data usage for a subscription (example INSERT).
INSERT INTO UsageRecords (sub_id, usage_date, data_used_gb)
VALUES (101, '2023-10-27', 5.5);

-- 4. Find subscriptions that have exceeded their data limit.
SELECT
    s.sub_id,
    s.user_id,
    p.plan_name,
    p.data_limit_gb,
    SUM(ur.data_used_gb) AS total_usage_this_month
FROM
    Subscriptions s
JOIN
    Plans p ON s.plan_id = p.plan_id
JOIN
    UsageRecords ur ON s.sub_id = ur.sub_id
WHERE
    STRFTIME('%Y-%m', ur.usage_date) = STRFTIME('%Y-%m', 'now') -- Current month
GROUP BY
    s.sub_id, p.data_limit_gb, p.plan_name, s.user_id
HAVING
    SUM(ur.data_used_gb) > p.data_limit_gb;

-- 5. Calculate the remaining data limit for each active subscription.
SELECT
    s.sub_id,
    s.user_id,
    p.plan_name,
    p.data_limit_gb - COALESCE(SUM(ur.data_used_gb), 0) AS remaining_data_gb
FROM
    Subscriptions s
JOIN
    Plans p ON s.plan_id = p.plan_id
LEFT JOIN
    UsageRecords ur ON s.sub_id = ur.sub_id AND STRFTIME('%Y-%m', ur.usage_date) = STRFTIME('%Y-%m', 'now')
WHERE
    s.end_date >= DATE('now') -- Active subscriptions
GROUP BY
    s.sub_id, s.user_id, p.plan_name, p.data_limit_gb;

text_es: Schema: Employees (employee_id, employee_name, manager_id), TimeOffTypes (type_id, type_name), TimeOffRequests (request_id, employee_id, type_id, start_date, end_date, status, approved_by_manager_id). Queries: 1. List all pending time off requests for an employee. 2. Find all time off requests awaiting approval from a specific manager. 3. Submit a new time off request. 4. Approve a time off request. 5. Get the total number of days requested per time off type.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all pending time off requests for an employee.
SELECT
    TOR.request_id,
    TOR.start_date,
    TOR.end_date,
    TOT.type_name
FROM
    TimeOffRequests AS TOR
JOIN
    TimeOffTypes AS TOT ON TOR.type_id = TOT.type_id
WHERE
    TOR.employee_id = @employee_id
    AND TOR.status = 'Pending';

-- 2. Find all time off requests awaiting approval from a specific manager.
SELECT
    TOR.request_id,
    E.employee_name AS employee_requesting,
    TOT.type_name,
    TOR.start_date,
    TOR.end_date
FROM
    TimeOffRequests AS TOR
JOIN
    Employees AS E ON TOR.employee_id = E.employee_id
JOIN
    TimeOffTypes AS TOT ON TOR.type_id = TOT.type_id
WHERE
    TOR.status = 'Pending'
    AND E.manager_id = @manager_id;

-- 3. Submit a new time off request.
INSERT INTO TimeOffRequests (employee_id, type_id, start_date, end_date, status)
VALUES (@employee_id, @type_id, @start_date, @end_date, 'Pending');

-- 4. Approve a time off request.
UPDATE TimeOffRequests
SET status = 'Approved', approved_by_manager_id = @approving_manager_id
WHERE request_id = @request_id
AND status = 'Pending'; -- Ensure only pending requests can be approved.

-- 5. Get the total number of days requested per time off type.
SELECT
    TOT.type_name,
    SUM(JULIANDAY(TOR.end_date) - JULIANDAY(TOR.start_date) + 1) AS total_days_requested
FROM
    TimeOffRequests AS TOR
JOIN
    TimeOffTypes AS TOT ON TOR.type_id = TOT.type_id
GROUP BY
    TOT.type_name;

text_es: Schema: MenuItems (item_id, item_name, description, price), Days (day_id, day_name), DailyMenu (daily_menu_id, day_id, item_id). Queries: 1. List all menu items for a specific day. 2. Find all days a particular menu item is served. 3. Add a menu item to a specific day's menu. 4. Update the price of a menu item. 5. Get the count of times each menu item appears on the menu.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all menu items for a specific day (e.g., 'Monday')
SELECT
  MI.item_name,
  MI.description,
  MI.price
FROM MenuItems AS MI
JOIN DailyMenu AS DM
  ON MI.item_id = DM.item_id
JOIN Days AS D
  ON DM.day_id = D.day_id
WHERE
  D.day_name = 'Monday';

-- 2. Find all days a particular menu item is served (e.g., 'Pizza')
SELECT
  D.day_name
FROM Days AS D
JOIN DailyMenu AS DM
  ON D.day_id = DM.day_id
JOIN MenuItems AS MI
  ON DM.item_id = MI.item_id
WHERE
  MI.item_name = 'Pizza';

-- 3. Add a menu item to a specific day's menu (e.g., add 'Pasta' to 'Tuesday')
INSERT INTO DailyMenu (day_id, item_id)
SELECT
  D.day_id,
  MI.item_id
FROM Days AS D
JOIN MenuItems AS MI
  ON D.day_name = 'Tuesday' AND MI.item_name = 'Pasta';

-- 4. Update the price of a menu item (e.g., update 'Pizza' to 12.99)
UPDATE MenuItems
SET
  price = 12.99
WHERE
  item_name = 'Pizza';

-- 5. Get the count of times each menu item appears on the menu
SELECT
  MI.item_name,
  COUNT(DM.item_id) AS appearance_count
FROM MenuItems AS MI
LEFT JOIN DailyMenu AS DM
  ON MI.item_id = DM.item_id
GROUP BY
  MI.item_name
ORDER BY
  appearance_count DESC;
text_alt:

  MI.item_id = DM.item_id AND DM.day_id = D.day_id AND D.day_name = 'Monday';

-- 2. Find all days a particular menu item is served (e.g., 'Pizza')
SELECT
  D.day_name
FROM Days AS D, DailyMenu AS DM, MenuItems AS MI
WHERE
  D.day_id = DM.day_id AND DM.item_id = MI.item_id AND MI.item_name = 'Pizza';

-- 3. Add a menu item to a specific day's menu (e.g., add 'Pasta' to 'Tuesday')
INSERT INTO DailyMenu (day_id, item_id)
SELECT
  D.day_id,
  MI.item_id
FROM Days AS D, MenuItems AS MI
WHERE
  D.day_name = 'Tuesday' AND MI.item_name = 'Pasta';

-- 4. Update the price of a menu item (e.g., update 'Pizza' to 12.99)
UPDATE MenuItems
SET

WHERE
  item_name = 'Pizza';

SELECT
  MI.item_name,

FROM MenuItems AS MI LEFT JOIN DailyMenu AS DM
  ON MI.item_id = DM.item_id
GROUP BY
  MI.item_name
ORDER BY
  appearance_count DESC;

text_es: Schema: Events (event_id, event_name, event_date, ticket_price), Tickets (ticket_id, event_id, customer_id, purchase_date, quantity). Queries: 1. Get the total revenue for a specific event. 2. List all tickets purchased by a specific customer. 3. Record new ticket sales for an event. 4. Find events that are sold out (assuming a fixed capacity, not in schema). 5. Get the total number of tickets sold per event.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the total revenue for a specific event
SELECT
    SUM(T.quantity * E.ticket_price) AS total_revenue
FROM
    Tickets AS T
JOIN
    Events AS E ON T.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE
    E.event_name = 'Concert A';

-- 2. List all tickets purchased by a specific customer
SELECT
    T.ticket_id,
    E.event_name,
    T.purchase_date,
    T.quantity
FROM
    Tickets AS T
JOIN
    Events AS E ON T.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE
    T.customer_id = 101;

-- 3. Record new ticket sales for an event (example insert)
INSERT INTO Tickets (event_id, customer_id, purchase_date, quantity)
SELECT E.event_id, 102, CURRENT_DATE, 3
FROM Events AS E
WHERE E.event_name = 'Theater Play';

-- 4. Find events that are sold out (assuming a fixed capacity of 100 for all events)
SELECT
    E.event_name
FROM
    Events AS E
JOIN
    (SELECT event_id, SUM(quantity) AS tickets_sold FROM Tickets GROUP BY event_id) AS TS
ON E.event_id = TS.event_id
WHERE
    TS.tickets_sold >= 100;

-- 5. Get the total number of tickets sold per event
SELECT
    E.event_name,
    SUM(T.quantity) AS total_tickets_sold
FROM
    Events AS E
LEFT JOIN
    Tickets AS T ON E.event_id = T.event_id
GROUP BY
    E.event_name
ORDER BY
    E.event_name;

text_es: Schema: Alumni (alumnus_id, alumnus_name, graduation_year, email), Funds (fund_id, fund_name, description), Donations (donation_id, alumnus_id, fund_id, amount, donation_date). Queries: 1. Get the total donations to a specific fund. 2. List all donations made by a particular alumnus. 3. Record a new donation to a fund by an alumnus. 4. Find alumni from a specific graduation year who have donated. 5. Get the total donation amount from each alumnus.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the total donations to a specific fund.

FROM Donations AS d
JOIN Funds AS f ON d.fund_id = f.fund_id
WHERE f.fund_name = 'Scholarship Fund';

-- 2. List all donations made by a particular alumnus.
SELECT d.donation_id, d.amount, d.donation_date, f.fund_name
FROM Donations AS d
JOIN Alumni AS a ON d.alumnus_id = a.alumnus_id
JOIN Funds AS f ON d.fund_id = f.fund_id
WHERE a.alumnus_name = 'John Doe';

FROM Alumni AS a
JOIN Funds AS f ON f.fund_name = 'Research Fund'
WHERE a.alumnus_name = 'Jane Smith';

-- 4. Find alumni from a specific graduation year who have donated.

FROM Alumni AS a
JOIN Donations AS d ON a.alumnus_id = d.alumnus_id
WHERE a.graduation_year = 2005;

-- 5. Get the total donation amount from each alumnus.
SELECT a.alumnus_name, SUM(d.amount) AS total_donated
FROM Alumni AS a
LEFT JOIN Donations AS d ON a.alumnus_id = d.alumnus_id
GROUP BY a.alumnus_name
ORDER BY total_donated DESC;

text_es: Schema: Orders (order_id, customer_id, order_date, total_amount), Shipments (shipment_id, order_id, carrier_name, tracking_number, shipment_date, delivery_date, status). Queries: 1. Get the shipment status for a specific order. 2. List all shipments for a particular customer. 3. Record a new shipment for an order. 4. Find all 'in transit' shipments. 5. Get the average delivery time for each carrier.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the shipment status for a specific order.
SELECT S.status
FROM Shipments AS S
JOIN Orders AS O
ON S.order_id = O.order_id
WHERE O.order_id = 101;

-- 2. List all shipments for a particular customer.
SELECT S.shipment_id, S.carrier_name, S.status
FROM Shipments AS S
JOIN Orders AS O
ON S.order_id = O.order_id
WHERE O.customer_id = 201;

-- 3. Record a new shipment for an order.

VALUES (102, 'FedEx', 'TRK123456789', '2023-10-27', 'shipped');

FROM Shipments AS S
JOIN Orders AS O
ON S.order_id = O.order_id
WHERE S.status = 'in transit';

-- 5. Get the average delivery time for each carrier.
SELECT S.carrier_name, AVG(JULIANDAY(S.delivery_date) - JULIANDAY(S.shipment_date)) AS avg_delivery_days
FROM Shipments AS S
JOIN Orders AS O
ON S.order_id = O.order_id
WHERE S.delivery_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY S.carrier_name;
