text_es: Schema: Users (user_id, username), Metrics (metric_id, metric_name, unit_of_measure), Readings (reading_id, user_id, metric_id, reading_value, reading_date). Queries: 1. Get the latest reading for a specific metric for a user. 2. List all readings for a metric for a user, ordered by date. 3. Insert a new metric reading. 4. Find users whose average reading for a metric is above a threshold. 5. Get the average reading for each metric across all users.
text_nat:
-- 1. Get the latest reading for a specific metric for a user
SELECT
  r.reading_value,
  r.reading_date
FROM Readings AS r
JOIN Users AS u
  ON r.user_id = u.user_id
JOIN Metrics AS m
  ON r.metric_id = m.metric_id
WHERE
  u.username = 'some_username' AND m.metric_name = 'some_metric'
ORDER BY
  r.reading_date DESC
LIMIT 1;

-- 2. List all readings for a metric for a user, ordered by date
SELECT
  r.reading_value,
  r.reading_date
FROM Readings AS r
JOIN Users AS u
  ON r.user_id = u.user_id
JOIN Metrics AS m
  ON r.metric_id = m.metric_id
WHERE
  u.username = 'some_username' AND m.metric_name = 'some_metric'
ORDER BY
  r.reading_date ASC;

-- 3. Insert a new metric reading
INSERT INTO Readings (user_id, metric_id, reading_value, reading_date)
SELECT
  u.user_id,
  m.metric_id,
  123.45,
  CURRENT_DATE
FROM Users AS u
JOIN Metrics AS m
  ON m.metric_name = 'new_metric_name'
WHERE
  u.username = 'existing_username';

-- 4. Find users whose average reading for a metric is above a threshold
SELECT
  u.username
FROM Users AS u
JOIN Readings AS r
  ON u.user_id = r.user_id
JOIN Metrics AS m
  ON r.metric_id = m.metric_id
WHERE
  m.metric_name = 'target_metric'
GROUP BY
  u.user_id,
  u.username
HAVING
  AVG(r.reading_value) > 100;

-- 5. Get the average reading for each metric across all users
SELECT
  m.metric_name,
  AVG(r.reading_value) AS average_reading
FROM Metrics AS m
JOIN Readings AS r
  ON m.metric_id = r.metric_id
GROUP BY
  m.metric_id,
  m.metric_name;

  m.metric_id = r.metric_id

text_es: Schema: Posts (post_id, title, content, publish_date), Tags (tag_id, tag_name), PostTags (post_id, tag_id). Queries: 1. Find all posts associated with a specific tag. 2. List all tags for a particular post. 3. Add a tag to a post. 4. Remove a tag from a post. 5. Get the count of posts for each tag.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all posts associated with a specific tag (e.g., 'SQL')
SELECT P.post_id, P.title, P.content, P.publish_date
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN PostTags AS PT ON P.post_id = PT.post_id
JOIN Tags AS T ON PT.tag_id = T.tag_id
WHERE T.tag_name = 'SQL';

-- 2. List all tags for a particular post (e.g., post_id = 1)
SELECT T.tag_name
FROM Tags AS T
JOIN PostTags AS PT ON T.tag_id = PT.tag_id
JOIN Posts AS P ON PT.post_id = P.post_id
WHERE P.post_id = 1;

-- 3. Add a tag (e.g., tag_id = 3) to a post (e.g., post_id = 1)
INSERT INTO PostTags (post_id, tag_id)
VALUES (1, 3);

-- 4. Remove a tag (e.g., tag_id = 2) from a post (e.g., post_id = 1)
DELETE FROM PostTags
WHERE post_id = 1 AND tag_id = 2;

-- 5. Get the count of posts for each tag
SELECT T.tag_name, COUNT(PT.post_id) AS post_count
FROM Tags AS T
LEFT JOIN PostTags AS PT ON T.tag_id = PT.tag_id
GROUP BY T.tag_name
ORDER BY T.tag_name;

AND PT.tag_id = T.tag_id
AND T.tag_name = 'SQL';

FROM Tags AS T, PostTags AS PT, Posts AS P
WHERE T.tag_id = PT.tag_id

DELETE FROM PostTags

SELECT T.tag_name, COUNT(PT.post_id) AS post_count
FROM Tags AS T
LEFT JOIN PostTags AS PT ON T.tag_id = PT.tag_id
GROUP BY T.tag_name
ORDER BY T.tag_name;

text_es: Schema: Users (user_id, username), Recipes (recipe_id, recipe_name, prep_time_minutes), MealPlans (plan_id, user_id, plan_date, meal_type), MealPlanRecipes (plan_id, recipe_id). Queries: 1. List all recipes for a specific user's meal plan on a given date. 2. Find all meal plans that include a particular recipe. 3. Add a recipe to a user's meal plan for a specific day and meal type. 4. Remove a recipe from a meal plan. 5. Get the total estimated prep time for each user's meal plan on a specific date.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all recipes for a specific user's meal plan on a given date.
SELECT
    r.recipe_name,
    r.prep_time_minutes
FROM
    Users u
JOIN
    MealPlans mp ON u.user_id = mp.user_id
JOIN
    MealPlanRecipes mpr ON mp.plan_id = mpr.plan_id
JOIN
    Recipes r ON mpr.recipe_id = r.recipe_id
WHERE
    u.username = 'Alice' AND mp.plan_date = '2023-10-26';

-- 2. Find all meal plans that include a particular recipe.
SELECT
    mp.plan_id,
    u.username,
    mp.plan_date,
    mp.meal_type
FROM
    MealPlans mp
JOIN
    Users u ON mp.user_id = u.user_id
JOIN
    MealPlanRecipes mpr ON mp.plan_id = mpr.plan_id
JOIN
    Recipes r ON mpr.recipe_id = r.recipe_id
WHERE
    r.recipe_name = 'Spaghetti Carbonara';

-- 3. Add a recipe to a user's meal plan for a specific day and meal type.
INSERT INTO MealPlanRecipes (plan_id, recipe_id)
SELECT
    mp.plan_id,
    r.recipe_id
FROM
    MealPlans mp
JOIN
    Users u ON mp.user_id = u.user_id
JOIN
    Recipes r ON r.recipe_name = 'Chicken Stir-fry' -- Assuming 'Chicken Stir-fry' exists
WHERE
    u.username = 'Bob'
    AND mp.plan_date = '2023-10-27'
    AND mp.meal_type = 'Dinner';

-- 4. Remove a recipe from a meal plan.
DELETE FROM MealPlanRecipes
WHERE
    plan_id = (SELECT mp.plan_id FROM MealPlans mp JOIN Users u ON mp.user_id = u.user_id WHERE u.username = 'Alice' AND mp.plan_date = '2023-10-26' AND mp.meal_type = 'Lunch')
    AND recipe_id = (SELECT recipe_id FROM Recipes WHERE recipe_name = 'Garden Salad');

-- 5. Get the total estimated prep time for each user's meal plan on a specific date.
SELECT
    u.username,
    mp.plan_date,
    SUM(r.prep_time_minutes) AS total_prep_time_minutes
FROM
    Users u
JOIN
    MealPlans mp ON u.user_id = mp.user_id
JOIN
    MealPlanRecipes mpr ON mp.plan_id = mpr.plan_id
JOIN
    Recipes r ON mpr.recipe_id = r.recipe_id
WHERE
    mp.plan_date = '2023-10-26'
GROUP BY
    u.username, mp.plan_date;

2. Calculate the total quantity of a given product across all warehouses.
3. Add a new product to a warehouse's inventory.
4. Decrease the quantity of a product in a warehouse.
5. List all warehouses and the number of distinct products they store.
text_nat:
SELECT
  p.name,
  p.price,
  i.quantity
FROM Products AS p
JOIN Inventory AS i
  ON p.product_id = i.product_id
JOIN Warehouses AS w
  ON i.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
WHERE
  w.location = 'Central' AND i.quantity > 100;

SELECT
  SUM(i.quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM Inventory AS i
JOIN Products AS p
  ON i.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE
  p.name = 'Laptop';

  p.product_id,
  w.warehouse_id,
  50,
  NOW()
FROM Products AS p
JOIN Warehouses AS w
  ON p.name = 'Keyboard' AND w.location = 'East';

JOIN Products AS p
  ON i.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN Warehouses AS w
  ON i.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
SET
  i.quantity = i.quantity - 10
WHERE
  p.name = 'Monitor' AND w.location = 'West';

SELECT
  w.location,
  COUNT(DISTINCT i.product_id) AS distinct_products_count
FROM Warehouses AS w
LEFT JOIN Inventory AS i
  ON w.warehouse_id = i.warehouse_id

  w.location;

Queries:

text_nat:
-- 1. Find all available vehicles of a specific model

    r.start_date,
    r.end_date,
    r.total_cost

Schema: Patients (patient_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, date_of_birth DATE), Doctors (doctor_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, specialization VARCHAR), Appointments (appointment_id INT, patient_id INT, doctor_id INT, appointment_date DATETIME, status VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all appointments for a specific doctor on a given date.
2. List all patients who have an appointment with a particular doctor.
3. Schedule a new appointment.
4. Update an appointment's status to 'completed'.
5. Count the number of appointments per specialization.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all appointments for a specific doctor on a given date.
SELECT
  A.appointment_id,
  P.first_name AS patient_first_name,
  P.last_name AS patient_last_name,
  A.appointment_date,
  A.status
FROM Appointments AS A
JOIN Patients AS P
  ON A.patient_id = P.patient_id
JOIN Doctors AS D
  ON A.doctor_id = D.doctor_id
WHERE
  D.doctor_id = 1 AND DATE(A.appointment_date) = '2023-10-26';

-- 2. List all patients who have an appointment with a particular doctor.
SELECT DISTINCT
  P.patient_id,
  P.first_name,
  P.last_name
FROM Patients AS P
JOIN Appointments AS A
  ON P.patient_id = A.patient_id
JOIN Doctors AS D
  ON A.doctor_id = D.doctor_id
WHERE
  D.doctor_id = 1;

-- 3. Schedule a new appointment.
INSERT INTO Appointments (
  patient_id,
  doctor_id,
  appointment_date,
  status
)
VALUES
  (1, 2, '2023-11-15 10:00:00', 'scheduled');

-- 4. Update an appointment's status to 'completed'.
UPDATE
  Appointments
SET
  status = 'completed'
WHERE
  appointment_id = 1;

-- 5. Count the number of appointments per specialization.
SELECT
  D.specialization,
  COUNT(A.appointment_id) AS total_appointments
FROM Doctors AS D
LEFT JOIN Appointments AS A
  ON D.doctor_id = A.doctor_id
GROUP BY
  D.specialization;
text_alt:
-- 1. Find all appointments for a specific doctor on a given date.

  A.status
FROM Appointments AS A, Patients AS P, Doctors AS D
WHERE
  A.patient_id = P.patient_id AND A.doctor_id = D.doctor_id AND D.doctor_id = 1 AND DATE(A.appointment_date) = '2023-10-26';

-- 2. List all patients who have an appointment with a particular doctor.
SELECT DISTINCT
  P.patient_id,

WHERE
  P.patient_id = A.patient_id AND A.doctor_id = D.doctor_id AND D.doctor_id = 1;

-- 3. Schedule a new appointment.

  patient_id,

)

FROM Doctors AS D

  ON D.doctor_id = A.doctor_id
GROUP BY
  D.specialization;

Schema: Users (user_id INT, username VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Albums (album_id INT, user_id INT, title VARCHAR, created_at DATETIME), Photos (photo_id INT, album_id INT, filename VARCHAR, upload_date DATETIME, description TEXT).
Queries:
1. Find all photos in a specific album.
2. List all albums created by a particular user.
3. Upload a new photo to an album.
4. Update a photo's description.
5. Count the number of photos in each album.
text_nat:
-- Task 1: Find all photos in a specific album (e.g., album_id = 1)
SELECT
  p.photo_id,
  p.filename,
  p.upload_date,
  p.description
FROM Photos AS p
JOIN Albums AS a
  ON p.album_id = a.album_id
WHERE
  a.album_id = 1;

-- Task 2: List all albums created by a particular user (e.g., user_id = 1)
SELECT
  al.album_id,
  al.title,
  al.created_at
FROM Albums AS al
JOIN Users AS u
  ON al.user_id = u.user_id
WHERE
  u.user_id = 1;

-- Task 3: Upload a new photo to an album (e.g., album_id = 2)
INSERT INTO Photos (album_id, filename, upload_date, description)
  VALUES (2, 'new_image.jpg', '2023-10-27 10:00:00', 'A fresh new photo.');

-- Task 4: Update a photo's description (e.g., photo_id = 3)
UPDATE Photos AS p
SET
  description = 'Updated description for this photo.'
WHERE
  p.photo_id = 3;

-- Task 5: Count the number of photos in each album
SELECT
  a.album_id,
  a.title,
  COUNT(p.photo_id) AS photo_count
FROM Albums AS a
LEFT JOIN Photos AS p
  ON a.album_id = p.album_id
GROUP BY
  a.album_id,
  a.title
ORDER BY
  a.album_id;
text_alt:
-- Task 1: Find all photos in a specific album (e.g., album_id = 1)
SELECT
  p.photo_id,
  p.filename,
  p.upload_date,
  p.description
FROM Photos AS p, Albums AS a
WHERE
  p.album_id = a.album_id AND a.album_id = 1;

-- Task 2: List all albums created by a particular user (e.g., user_id = 1)
SELECT
  al.album_id,
  al.title,
  al.created_at
FROM Albums AS al, Users AS u
WHERE
  al.user_id = u.user_id AND u.user_id = 1;

-- Task 3: Upload a new photo to an album (e.g., album_id = 2)
INSERT INTO Photos (album_id, filename, upload_date, description)
  VALUES (2, 'new_image.jpg', '2023-10-27 10:00:00', 'A fresh new photo.');

-- Task 4: Update a photo's description (e.g., photo_id = 3)
UPDATE Photos AS p
SET
  description = 'Updated description for this photo.'
WHERE
  p.photo_id = 3;

-- Task 5: Count the number of photos in each album
SELECT
  a.album_id,
  a.title,
  COUNT(p.photo_id) AS photo_count
FROM Albums AS a
LEFT JOIN Photos AS p
  ON a.album_id = p.album_id
GROUP BY
  a.album_id,
  a.title
ORDER BY
  a.album_id;

Schema: Rooms (room_id INT, room_number VARCHAR, type VARCHAR, price_per_night DECIMAL, status VARCHAR), Guests (guest_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Bookings (booking_id INT, room_id INT, guest_id INT, check_in_date DATE, check_out_date DATE, total_price DECIMAL).
Queries:
1. Find all available rooms for a given date range.
2. List all bookings made by a specific guest.
3. Create a new room booking.
4. Update a room's status to 'occupied'.
5. Calculate the total revenue from bookings per room type.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all available rooms for a given date range
SELECT
    r.room_id,
    r.room_number,
    r.type,
    r.price_per_night
FROM
    Rooms r
LEFT JOIN
    Bookings b ON r.room_id = b.room_id
WHERE
    r.status = 'available' AND (
        b.booking_id IS NULL OR
        (
            '2023-10-26' >= b.check_out_date OR
            '2023-10-28' <= b.check_in_date
        )
    );

-- 2. List all bookings made by a specific guest
SELECT
    b.booking_id,
    r.room_number,
    b.check_in_date,
    b.check_out_date,
    b.total_price
FROM
    Bookings b
JOIN
    Rooms r ON b.room_id = r.room_id
JOIN
    Guests g ON b.guest_id = g.guest_id
WHERE
    g.first_name = 'John' AND g.last_name = 'Doe';

-- 3. Create a new room booking
INSERT INTO Bookings (room_id, guest_id, check_in_date, check_out_date, total_price)
SELECT
    r.room_id, g.guest_id, '2023-11-01', '2023-11-05',
    r.price_per_night * (JULIANDAY('2023-11-05') - JULIANDAY('2023-11-01'))
FROM
    Rooms r
JOIN
    Guests g ON g.first_name = 'Jane' AND g.last_name = 'Smith'
WHERE
    r.room_number = '101';

-- 4. Update a room's status to 'occupied'
UPDATE Rooms
SET status = 'occupied'
WHERE room_id = (SELECT room_id FROM Bookings WHERE booking_id = 101);

-- 5. Calculate the total revenue from bookings per room type
SELECT
    r.type,
    SUM(b.total_price) AS total_revenue
FROM
    Rooms r
JOIN
    Bookings b ON r.room_id = b.room_id
GROUP BY
    r.type;

Schema: Items (item_id INT, name VARCHAR, weight DECIMAL, dimensions VARCHAR), Locations (location_id INT, warehouse_name VARCHAR, aisle VARCHAR, rack VARCHAR), ItemLocations (item_id INT, location_id INT, quantity INT, last_moved DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all items stored in a specific aisle of a warehouse.
2. List all locations where a particular item is stored.
3. Add new stock of an item to a location.
4. Move an item from one location to another.
5. Count the total quantity of each item across all locations.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all items stored in a specific aisle of a warehouse.
SELECT
    I.name,
    I.weight,
    I.dimensions
FROM
    Items I
JOIN
    ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id
JOIN
    Locations L ON IL.location_id = L.location_id
WHERE
    L.warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND L.aisle = 'A1';

-- 2. List all locations where a particular item is stored.
SELECT
    L.warehouse_name,
    L.aisle,
    L.rack,
    IL.quantity
FROM
    Locations L
JOIN
    ItemLocations IL ON L.location_id = IL.location_id
JOIN
    Items I ON IL.item_id = I.item_id
WHERE
    I.name = 'Laptop';

-- 3. Add new stock of an item to a location (assuming item_id = 1, location_id = 101, quantity = 5).
INSERT INTO ItemLocations (item_id, location_id, quantity, last_moved)
VALUES (1, 101, 5, NOW())
ON CONFLICT (item_id, location_id) DO UPDATE SET
    quantity = ItemLocations.quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity,
    last_moved = EXCLUDED.last_moved;

-- 4. Move an item from one location to another (move 2 units of item_id 1 from location 101 to location 102).
UPDATE ItemLocations
SET quantity = quantity - 2, last_moved = NOW()
WHERE item_id = 1 AND location_id = 101;

INSERT INTO ItemLocations (item_id, location_id, quantity, last_moved)
VALUES (1, 102, 2, NOW())
ON CONFLICT (item_id, location_id) DO UPDATE SET
    quantity = ItemLocations.quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity,
    last_moved = EXCLUDED.last_moved;

-- 5. Count the total quantity of each item across all locations.
SELECT
    I.name,
    SUM(IL.quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM
    Items I
JOIN
    ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id
GROUP BY
    I.name
ORDER BY
    I.name;

    quantity = ItemLocations.quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity,
    last_moved = EXCLUDED.last_moved;

-- 4. Move an item from one location to another (move 2 units of item_id 1 from location 101 to location 102).
UPDATE ItemLocations
SET quantity = quantity - 2, last_moved = NOW()
WHERE item_id = 1 AND location_id = 101;

INSERT INTO ItemLocations (item_id, location_id, quantity, last_moved)
VALUES (1, 102, 2, NOW())
ON CONFLICT (item_id, location_id) DO UPDATE SET
    quantity = ItemLocations.quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity,
    last_moved = EXCLUDED.last_moved;

-- 5. Count the total quantity of each item across all locations.
SELECT
    I.name,
    SUM(IL.quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM
    Items I,
    ItemLocations IL
WHERE
    I.item_id = IL.item_id
GROUP BY
    I.name
ORDER BY
    I.name;

-- 1. Find all available pets of a specific species (e.g., 'dog')

SELECT P.name, P.species, P.breed, A.adoption_date
FROM Pets AS P
JOIN Adoptions AS A ON P.pet_id = A.pet_id
JOIN Adopters AS AD ON A.adopter_id = AD.adopter_id
WHERE AD.first_name = 'John' AND AD.last_name = 'Doe';

SET status = 'adopted'
WHERE pet_id = 1;

GROUP BY species;

Queries:
1. Find all visits for a specific patient.
2. List all patients seen by a particular doctor.
3. Record a new patient visit.
4. Update a patient's diagnosis for a visit.
5. Count the number of visits per doctor's specialty.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all visits for a specific patient.
SELECT
  v.visit_id,
  v.visit_date,
  v.diagnosis,
  d.first_name AS doctor_first_name,
  d.last_name AS doctor_last_name
FROM Visits AS v
JOIN Patients AS p
  ON v.patient_id = p.patient_id
JOIN Doctors AS d
  ON v.doctor_id = d.doctor_id
WHERE
  p.patient_id = 1;

-- 2. List all patients seen by a particular doctor.
SELECT DISTINCT
  p.first_name,
  p.last_name,
  p.date_of_birth,
  p.gender
FROM Patients AS p
JOIN Visits AS v
  ON p.patient_id = v.patient_id
JOIN Doctors AS d
  ON v.doctor_id = d.doctor_id
WHERE
  d.doctor_id = 101;

-- 3. Record a new patient visit.
INSERT INTO Visits (patient_id, doctor_id, visit_date, diagnosis)
VALUES
  (1, 101, '2023-11-01 10:00:00', 'Common cold');

-- 4. Update a patient's diagnosis for a visit.
UPDATE Visits
SET
  diagnosis = 'Seasonal flu'
WHERE
  visit_id = 5;

-- 5. Count the number of visits per doctor's specialty.
SELECT
  d.specialty,
  COUNT(v.visit_id) AS number_of_visits
FROM Doctors AS d
JOIN Visits AS v
  ON d.doctor_id = v.doctor_id
GROUP BY
  d.specialty
ORDER BY
  number_of_visits DESC;

JOIN Guests AS G ON EG.guest_id = G.guest_id

Queries:
1. Find all matches played by a specific team.
2. List all players on a particular team.
3. Record a new match score.
4. Update a player's position.
5. Calculate the total wins for each team.
text_nat:
SELECT * FROM Matches m JOIN Teams t ON m.home_team_id = t.team_id OR m.away_team_id = t.team_id WHERE t.name = 'Barcelona';

SELECT * FROM Players p JOIN Teams t ON p.team_id = t.team_id WHERE t.name = 'Real Madrid';

UPDATE Matches SET home_score = 3, away_score = 1 WHERE match_id = 101;

UPDATE Players SET position = 'Midfielder' WHERE player_id = 5;

SELECT
    t.name AS team_name,
    COUNT(CASE
        WHEN m.home_team_id = t.team_id AND m.home_score > m.away_score THEN 1
        WHEN m.away_team_id = t.team_id AND m.away_score > m.home_score THEN 1
        ELSE NULL
    END) AS total_wins
FROM
    Teams t
LEFT JOIN
    Matches m ON t.team_id = m.home_team_id OR t.team_id = m.away_team_id
GROUP BY
    t.team_id, t.name
ORDER BY
    total_wins DESC;

        WHEN m.home_team_id = t.team_id AND m.home_score > m.away_score THEN 1
        WHEN m.away_team_id = t.team_id AND m.away_score > m.home_score THEN 1
        ELSE NULL
    END) AS total_wins
FROM

GROUP BY

Queries:
1. Find all donations made by a specific donor.
2. List all donations for a particular campaign.
3. Record a new donation.
4. Update a campaign's target amount.
5. Calculate the total amount raised for each campaign.
text_nat:
SELECT d.donation_id, d.amount, d.donation_date
FROM Donations d
JOIN Donors dr ON d.donor_id = dr.donor_id
WHERE dr.donor_id = 1;

SELECT d.donation_id, d.amount, d.donation_date, dr.name AS donor_name
FROM Donations d
JOIN Campaigns c ON d.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
JOIN Donors dr ON d.donor_id = dr.donor_id
WHERE c.campaign_id = 2;

INSERT INTO Donations (donor_id, campaign_id, amount, donation_date)
VALUES (1, 2, 50.00, '2023-11-01 10:30:00');

UPDATE Campaigns
SET target_amount = 15000.00
WHERE campaign_id = 1;

SELECT c.name AS campaign_name, SUM(d.amount) AS total_raised
FROM Campaigns c
LEFT JOIN Donations d ON c.campaign_id = d.campaign_id
GROUP BY c.name;
text_alt:
SELECT d.donation_id, d.amount, d.donation_date
FROM Donations d, Donors dr 
WHERE d.donor_id = dr.donor_id
AND dr.donor_id = 1;

SELECT d.donation_id, d.amount, d.donation_date, dr.name AS donor_name
FROM Donations d, Campaigns c, Donors dr 
WHERE d.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
AND d.donor_id = dr.donor_id
AND c.campaign_id = 2;

INSERT INTO Donations (donor_id, campaign_id, amount, donation_date)
VALUES (1, 2, 50.00, '2023-11-01 10:30:00');

UPDATE Campaigns
SET target_amount = 15000.00
WHERE campaign_id = 1;

SELECT c.name AS campaign_name, SUM(d.amount) AS total_raised
FROM Campaigns c
LEFT JOIN Donations d ON c.campaign_id = d.campaign_id
GROUP BY c.name;

Schema: Vehicles (vehicle_id INT, make VARCHAR, model VARCHAR, year INT, license_plate VARCHAR), Services (service_id INT, vehicle_id INT, service_date DATE, description TEXT, cost DECIMAL), Mechanics (mechanic_id INT, name VARCHAR, specialization VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all services performed on a specific vehicle.
2. List all vehicles serviced by a particular mechanic.
3. Record a new service for a vehicle.
4. Update the cost of a service.
5. Calculate the total service cost for each vehicle.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all services performed on a specific vehicle.
SELECT s.service_id, s.service_date, s.description, s.cost
FROM Services s
JOIN Vehicles v ON s.vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id
WHERE v.license_plate = 'ABC1234';

-- 2. List all vehicles serviced by a particular mechanic (assuming a linking table ServiceMechanics for many-to-many relationship)
-- For this simplified schema, let's assume a mechanic is associated with a service directly, or we create a linking table.
-- Since no linking table is provided, we'll assume a direct mechanic_id in Services for this query, or indicate it's not possible directly.
-- If ServiceMechanics (service_id, mechanic_id) existed:
/*
SELECT DISTINCT v.make, v.model, v.license_plate
FROM Vehicles v
JOIN Services s ON v.vehicle_id = s.vehicle_id
JOIN ServiceMechanics sm ON s.service_id = sm.service_id
JOIN Mechanics m ON sm.mechanic_id = m.mechanic_id
WHERE m.name = 'John Doe';
*/
-- Without a linking table, this query cannot be directly fulfilled with the given schema.
-- Let's re-interpret: if a service has a mechanic associated, it's not in the schema.
-- If we assume the question implies listing vehicles that *could be* serviced by a mechanic based on specializations, it's not possible.
-- Let's assume a simplified scenario where we want to list all services and the vehicles associated, to show JOIN usage.
SELECT v.make, v.model, s.service_date, s.description
FROM Vehicles v
JOIN Services s ON v.vehicle_id = s.vehicle_id;


-- 3. Record a new service for a vehicle.
INSERT INTO Services (vehicle_id, service_date, description, cost)
SELECT v.vehicle_id, '2023-10-26', 'Tire Rotation', 75.00
FROM Vehicles v
WHERE v.license_plate = 'XYZ987';

-- 4. Update the cost of a service.
UPDATE Services
SET cost = 150.00
WHERE service_id = 101; -- Assuming service_id 101 exists

-- 5. Calculate the total service cost for each vehicle.
SELECT v.make, v.model, SUM(s.cost) AS total_cost
FROM Vehicles v
JOIN Services s ON v.vehicle_id = s.vehicle_id
GROUP BY v.vehicle_id, v.make, v.model;

SELECT v.make, v.model, s.service_date, s.description

Schema: Customers (customer_id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Plans (plan_id INT, name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL, duration_months INT), Subscriptions (subscription_id INT, customer_id INT, plan_id INT, start_date DATE, end_date DATE, status VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all active subscriptions for a specific customer.
2. List all customers subscribed to a particular plan.
3. Create a new subscription.
4. Update a subscription's status to 'cancelled'.
5. Count the number of active subscriptions per plan.
text_nat:
SELECT
  s.subscription_id,
  s.start_date,
  s.end_date,
  p.name AS plan_name,
  p.price
FROM Subscriptions AS s
JOIN Plans AS p
  ON s.plan_id = p.plan_id
WHERE
  s.customer_id = 1
  AND s.status = 'active';

SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.name,
  c.email
FROM Customers AS c
JOIN Subscriptions AS s
  ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id
JOIN Plans AS p
  ON s.plan_id = p.plan_id
WHERE
  p.name = 'Premium Plan';

INSERT INTO Subscriptions (customer_id, plan_id, start_date, end_date, status)
VALUES (
  2,
  (
    SELECT
      plan_id
    FROM Plans
    WHERE
      name = 'Standard Plan'
  ),
  '2023-10-01',
  '2024-09-30',
  'active'
);

UPDATE Subscriptions
SET
  status = 'cancelled'
WHERE
  subscription_id = 101;

SELECT
  p.name AS plan_name,
  COUNT(s.subscription_id) AS active_subscriptions_count
FROM Plans AS p
LEFT JOIN Subscriptions AS s
  ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id
WHERE
  s.status = 'active'
GROUP BY
  p.name;
text_alt:
SELECT
  s.subscription_id,
  s.start_date,
  s.end_date,
  p.name AS plan_name,
  p.price
FROM Subscriptions AS s, Plans AS p
WHERE
  s.plan_id = p.plan_id
  AND s.customer_id = 1
  AND s.status = 'active';

SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.name,
  c.email
FROM Customers AS c, Subscriptions AS s, Plans AS p
WHERE
  c.customer_id = s.customer_id
  AND s.plan_id = p.plan_id
  AND p.name = 'Premium Plan';

INSERT INTO Subscriptions (customer_id, plan_id, start_date, end_date, status)
VALUES (
  2,
  (
    SELECT
      plan_id
    FROM Plans
    WHERE
      name = 'Standard Plan'
  ),
  '2023-10-01',
  '2024-09-30',
  'active'
);

UPDATE Subscriptions
SET
  status = 'cancelled'
WHERE
  subscription_id = 101;

SELECT
  p.name AS plan_name,
  COUNT(s.subscription_id) AS active_subscriptions_count
FROM Plans AS p
LEFT JOIN Subscriptions AS s
  ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id
WHERE
  s.status = 'active'
GROUP BY
  p.name;

Schema: Projects (project_id INT, name VARCHAR, manager_id INT, start_date DATE, end_date DATE), Employees (employee_id INT, name VARCHAR, position VARCHAR), ProjectAssignments (project_id INT, employee_id INT, role VARCHAR, start_date DATE, end_date DATE).
Queries:
1. Find all employees assigned to a specific project.
2. List all projects managed by a particular employee.
3. Assign an employee to a project.
4. Update an employee's role on a project.
5. Count the number of employees per project.
text_nat:
SELECT
  e.employee_id,
  e.name AS employee_name,
  pa.role
FROM Employees AS e
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS pa
  ON e.employee_id = pa.employee_id
WHERE
  pa.project_id = 1;

SELECT
  p.project_id,
  p.name AS project_name,
  p.start_date,
  p.end_date
FROM Projects AS p
JOIN Employees AS e
  ON p.manager_id = e.employee_id
WHERE
  e.employee_id = 101;

INSERT INTO ProjectAssignments (project_id, employee_id, role, start_date, end_date)
VALUES
  (2, 103, 'Developer', '2023-01-15', '2023-06-15');

UPDATE ProjectAssignments
SET
  role = 'Lead Developer'
FROM ProjectAssignments AS pa
JOIN Employees AS e
  ON pa.employee_id = e.employee_id
WHERE
  pa.project_id = 2 AND pa.employee_id = 103;

SELECT
  p.name AS project_name,
  COUNT(pa.employee_id) AS number_of_employees
FROM Projects AS p
LEFT JOIN ProjectAssignments AS pa
  ON p.project_id = pa.project_id
GROUP BY
  p.name
ORDER BY
  number_of_employees DESC;
text_alt:
SELECT
  e.employee_id,
  e.name AS employee_name,
  pa.role
FROM Employees AS e, ProjectAssignments AS pa
WHERE e.employee_id = pa.employee_id
  AND pa.project_id = 1;

SELECT
  p.project_id,
  p.name AS project_name,
  p.start_date,
  p.end_date
FROM Projects AS p, Employees AS e
WHERE p.manager_id = e.employee_id
  AND e.employee_id = 101;

INSERT INTO ProjectAssignments (project_id, employee_id, role, start_date, end_date)
VALUES
  (2, 103, 'Developer', '2023-01-15', '2023-06-15');

UPDATE ProjectAssignments
SET
  role = 'Lead Developer'
FROM ProjectAssignments AS pa, Employees AS e
WHERE pa.employee_id = e.employee_id
  AND pa.project_id = 2 AND pa.employee_id = 103;

SELECT
  p.name AS project_name,
  COUNT(pa.employee_id) AS number_of_employees
FROM Projects AS p
LEFT JOIN ProjectAssignments AS pa
  ON p.project_id = pa.project_id
GROUP BY
  p.name
ORDER BY
  number_of_employees DESC;

Schema: Users (user_id INT, username VARCHAR, registration_date DATETIME, last_login DATETIME), Pages (page_id INT, url VARCHAR, title VARCHAR), PageViews (view_id INT, user_id INT, page_id INT, view_date DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all pages viewed by a specific user.
2. List the top 5 most viewed pages.
3. Record a new page view.
4. Update a user's last login date.
5. Count the total page views for each user.
text_nat:
SELECT P.title, P.url
FROM Pages AS P
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
WHERE PV.user_id = 1;

SELECT P.title, P.url, COUNT(PV.page_id) AS view_count
FROM Pages AS P
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
GROUP BY P.page_id, P.title, P.url
ORDER BY view_count DESC
LIMIT 5;

INSERT INTO PageViews (user_id, page_id, view_date)
VALUES (1, 3, NOW());

UPDATE Users
SET last_login = NOW()
WHERE user_id = 1;

SELECT U.username, COUNT(PV.view_id) AS total_views
FROM Users AS U
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON U.user_id = PV.user_id
GROUP BY U.user_id, U.username;
text_alt:
SELECT P.title, P.url
FROM Pages AS P, PageViews AS PV
WHERE P.page_id = PV.page_id
AND PV.user_id = 1;

SELECT P.title, P.url, COUNT(PV.page_id) AS view_count
FROM Pages AS P, PageViews AS PV
WHERE P.page_id = PV.page_id
GROUP BY P.page_id, P.title, P.url
ORDER BY view_count DESC
LIMIT 5;

INSERT INTO PageViews (user_id, page_id, view_date)
VALUES (1, 3, NOW());

UPDATE Users
SET last_login = NOW()
WHERE user_id = 1;

SELECT U.username, COUNT(PV.view_id) AS total_views
FROM Users AS U, PageViews AS PV
WHERE U.user_id = PV.user_id
GROUP BY U.user_id, U.username;

Schema: Equipment (equipment_id INT, name VARCHAR, type VARCHAR, purchase_date DATE, status VARCHAR, department_id INT), Departments (department_id INT, name VARCHAR, location VARCHAR), Maintenance (maintenance_id INT, equipment_id INT, maintenance_date DATE, description TEXT, cost DECIMAL).
Queries:
1. Find all equipment in a specific department needing maintenance.
2. List all maintenance records for a particular piece of equipment.
3. Add a new piece of equipment.
4. Update an equipment's status to 'in repair'.
5. Calculate the total maintenance cost per equipment type.
text_nat:
SELECT
  E.name AS equipment_name,
  E.type,
  E.status,
  D.name AS department_name
FROM Equipment AS E
JOIN Departments AS D
  ON E.department_id = D.department_id
WHERE
  D.name = 'Engineering' AND E.status = 'needs maintenance';

SELECT
  M.maintenance_date,
  M.description,
  M.cost
FROM Maintenance AS M
JOIN Equipment AS E
  ON M.equipment_id = E.equipment_id
WHERE
  E.name = 'Server Rack 01';

INSERT INTO Equipment (name, type, purchase_date, status, department_id)
  VALUES ('New Drill Press', 'Machine', '2023-10-26', 'operational', (
    SELECT
      department_id
    FROM Departments
    WHERE
      name = 'Manufacturing'
  ));

UPDATE Equipment
SET
  status = 'in repair'
WHERE
  equipment_id = 101;

SELECT
  E.type,
  SUM(M.cost) AS total_maintenance_cost
FROM Equipment AS E
JOIN Maintenance AS M
  ON E.equipment_id = M.equipment_id
GROUP BY
  E.type;
text_alt:
SELECT
  E.name AS equipment_name,
  E.type,
  E.status,
  D.name AS department_name
FROM Equipment AS E, Departments AS D
WHERE E.department_id = D.department_id
  AND D.name = 'Engineering' AND E.status = 'needs maintenance';

SELECT
  M.maintenance_date,
  M.description,
  M.cost
FROM Maintenance AS M, Equipment AS E
WHERE M.equipment_id = E.equipment_id
  AND E.name = 'Server Rack 01';

INSERT INTO Equipment (name, type, purchase_date, status, department_id)
  VALUES ('New Drill Press', 'Machine', '2023-10-26', 'operational', (
    SELECT
      department_id
    FROM Departments
    WHERE
      name = 'Manufacturing'
  ));

UPDATE Equipment
SET
  status = 'in repair'
WHERE
  equipment_id = 101;

SELECT
  E.type,
  SUM(M.cost) AS total_maintenance_cost
FROM Equipment AS E, Maintenance AS M
WHERE E.equipment_id = M.equipment_id
GROUP BY
  E.type;

Schema: Students (student_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, class_id INT), Classes (class_id INT, name VARCHAR, teacher_id INT), Attendance (attendance_id INT, student_id INT, class_id INT, attendance_date DATE, status VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all attendance records for a specific student.
2. List all students marked 'Absent' for a particular class on a given date.
3. Record a student's attendance for a class.
4. Update an attendance record's status.
5. Count the total 'Present' records for each class.
text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM Attendance
WHERE student_id = 1;

SELECT
    S.first_name,
    S.last_name
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Attendance AS A
    ON S.student_id = A.student_id
JOIN Classes AS C
    ON A.class_id = C.class_id
WHERE
    C.name = 'Math' AND A.attendance_date = '2023-10-26' AND A.status = 'Absent';

INSERT INTO Attendance (student_id, class_id, attendance_date, status)
VALUES (1, 101, '2023-10-27', 'Present');

UPDATE Attendance
SET
    status = 'Present'
WHERE
    attendance_id = 5 AND student_id = 1;

SELECT
    C.name,
    COUNT(A.attendance_id) AS total_present
FROM Classes AS C
LEFT JOIN Attendance AS A
    ON C.class_id = A.class_id
WHERE
    A.status = 'Present'
GROUP BY
    C.name;
text_alt:
SELECT *
FROM Attendance
WHERE student_id = 1;

SELECT
    S.first_name,
    S.last_name
FROM Students AS S, Attendance AS A, Classes AS C
WHERE S.student_id = A.student_id
AND A.class_id = C.class_id
AND
    C.name = 'Math' AND A.attendance_date = '2023-10-26' AND A.status = 'Absent';

INSERT INTO Attendance (student_id, class_id, attendance_date, status)
VALUES (1, 101, '2023-10-27', 'Present');

UPDATE Attendance
SET
    status = 'Present'
WHERE
    attendance_id = 5 AND student_id = 1;

SELECT
    C.name,
    COUNT(A.attendance_id) AS total_present
FROM Classes AS C
LEFT JOIN Attendance AS A
    ON C.class_id = A.class_id
WHERE
    A.status = 'Present'
GROUP BY
    C.name;

Schema: Employees (employee_id INT, name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR), Courses (course_id INT, title VARCHAR, duration_hours INT), TrainingRecords (record_id INT, employee_id INT, course_id INT, completion_date DATE, score INT).
Queries:
1. Find all training courses completed by a specific employee.
2. List all employees who completed a particular course with a score above 80.
3. Record a new training completion for an employee.
4. Update an employee's score for a completed course.
5. Calculate the average score for each course.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all training courses completed by a specific employee (e.g., employee_id = 1)
SELECT
    C.title,
    C.duration_hours,
    TR.completion_date,
    TR.score
FROM
    TrainingRecords TR
JOIN
    Courses C ON TR.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE
    TR.employee_id = 1;

-- 2. List all employees who completed a particular course (e.g., course_id = 101) with a score above 80
SELECT
    E.name,
    E.department,
    TR.score
FROM
    Employees E
JOIN
    TrainingRecords TR ON E.employee_id = TR.employee_id
WHERE
    TR.course_id = 101 AND TR.score > 80;

-- 3. Record a new training completion for an employee (e.g., employee 2, course 102, date '2023-10-26', score 92)
INSERT INTO TrainingRecords (employee_id, course_id, completion_date, score)
VALUES (2, 102, '2023-10-26', 92);

-- 4. Update an employee's score for a completed course (e.g., employee 1, course 101, new score 95)
UPDATE TrainingRecords
SET score = 95
WHERE employee_id = 1 AND course_id = 101;

-- 5. Calculate the average score for each course
SELECT
    C.title,
    AVG(TR.score) AS average_score
FROM
    Courses C
LEFT JOIN
    TrainingRecords TR ON C.course_id = TR.course_id
GROUP BY
    C.title;
text_alt:
-- 1. Find all training courses completed by a specific employee (e.g., employee_id = 1)
SELECT
    C.title,
    C.duration_hours,
    TR.completion_date,
    TR.score
FROM
    TrainingRecords TR,
    Courses C
WHERE
    TR.course_id = C.course_id AND TR.employee_id = 1;

-- 2. List all employees who completed a particular course (e.g., course_id = 101) with a score above 80
SELECT
    E.name,
    E.department,
    TR.score
FROM
    Employees E,
    TrainingRecords TR
WHERE
    E.employee_id = TR.employee_id AND TR.course_id = 101 AND TR.score > 80;

-- 3. Record a new training completion for an employee (e.g., employee 2, course 102, date '2023-10-26', score 92)
INSERT INTO TrainingRecords (employee_id, course_id, completion_date, score)
VALUES (2, 102, '2023-10-26', 92);

-- 4. Update an employee's score for a completed course (e.g., employee 1, course 101, new score 95)
UPDATE TrainingRecords
SET score = 95
WHERE employee_id = 1 AND course_id = 101;

-- 5. Calculate the average score for each course
SELECT
    C.title,
    AVG(TR.score) AS average_score
FROM
    Courses C
LEFT JOIN
    TrainingRecords TR ON C.course_id = TR.course_id
GROUP BY
    C.title;
